title: Review: everything that changed goes to the AI whole, in one request; past [explain] max_chars it is an error
description: Decision docair-8l6.34, reviewed and replaced: by default every change goes to the model, however many. No cap on the lists that point at parts (new, gone, code changed, between, lines, flows), no cut of a part's text (MAX_PART_TEXT 4,000, MAX_PIECE_TEXT 20,000), of changed files no part holds (MAX_FILE, MAX_FILES), of commit message bodies (MAX_BODY) or of changed docs (MAX_DOC, MAX_DOCS). The review is one request; the only limit is the model's input, [explain] max_chars (default 1,000,000, docair-8l6.70). A review whose input passes it is not split: docair explain and the served job fail with an error that says how many characters the review needs, the limit, and how to raise it or review a smaller range. So splitting goes: the batches, max_requests, AT_ONCE, the told list of other requests' pieces (elsewhere, leave_elsewhere) and the merge of changes that came back twice; the last request stays only for pieces left in no change (docair-8l6.69). To settle when building: whether generated files (lock files, the beads export, review stores) stay out as now, as not the change's code. Docs: EXPLAIN 7 and 9.2, SPEC explain row.
close_reason: One streamed request (client::chat_streamed, complete_changes), nothing cut, an error past max_chars; batches, max_requests, AT_ONCE, the told list and merge_same gone; real model on the shop: changes streamed before the answer ended; e2e 71/71, docair check 0/0

title: Review: the size of a request is [explain] max_chars, default 1,000,000 characters
description: Decision docair-8l6.8, reviewed: the 60,000-character cap per review request came from when the AI got only summaries; now it reads whole part texts, so docair's own change needed 6 requests and a merge, while the model takes about a million characters in one chat request. The cap becomes a setting, [explain] max_chars, default 1,000,000; most reviews then fit one request, so the AI sees every piece together (no merge of the same change, no pieces of other requests). Splitting, the told list and the last request stay for reviews beyond it. MAX_ELSEWHERE follows as a quarter of it. Docs: EXPLAIN 7, SPEC explain row, docair.toml reference.
notes: Reviewed with 8l6.34: max_chars is the only limit of a review's input; a review past it is an error, not split (docair-8l6.79).
close_reason: [explain] max_chars (default 1,000,000) and reasoning (default low) in ExplainSettings; ReviewSettings::of; tests in explain and project.rs; e2e 71/71, docair check 0/0

title: A review older than the change shows its old changes and hides the new pieces, with no way to review again
description: When the working tree (or B) changes after docair explain stored its review, the page shows the stored changes as they were. The pieces no stored change holds, not in 'other' and not 'left', appear in no change, and the page neither says the review is out of date nor offers to review again (the button shows only without a review). Pieces 'left' (beyond max_requests) are not shown either. Fix: every piece is a change: such pieces show as changes of their own in docair's words, marked 'newer than the review' or 'not asked: the run reached its limit of requests'; the list says how many pieces the review does not cover and, served, offers '✦ Review again' with the job's progress.
close_reason: Pieces left or newer than the review are changes of their own in docair's words; the list says the review is older and offers Review again; a stored change with no piece left is left out; tests/page.rs; e2e 71/71

title: Review the changes seems to do nothing: its progress hides in the button, and no change shows until every request is back
description: Clicking '✦ Review the changes' on a served page starts an explain job. The page shows the job only as the button's label, polled every 1.5 s, and nothing of the review until every request has answered and the page reloads; on docair's own change that is minutes of an unchanged-looking page. Fix: each answer is bound as soon as those before it are (the same order as before, so the review does not change), and the changes bound so far go out with the progress (ExplainProgress.found). The job's JSON carries html: a bar of the requests answered with the job's words, then each change made so far (title, pieces, found off, why). The page shows it under the button while the job runs, then reloads.
notes: Built: explain_with binds each answer as soon as those before it are (RunState, bind_answer; same order, same review), ExplainProgress.found carries the changes so far; the server's job JSON has html (job_html: a bar of the requests answered with the job's words, then each change so far: title, pieces, found off, why); the page shows it under the button every second and reloads when done; docair explain prints each change as it is made. Tests: project::tests::a_running_review_shows_its_changes_so_far; e2e cli.spec: the job has html with a bar and found, and the button on a served page shows the bar, then the page reloads with the review. SPEC changes section and API row, EXPLAIN 8.
close_reason: Answers bound as soon as those before are; the job's html shows a bar and the changes so far under the button; docair explain prints each change as made; test a_running_review_shows_its_changes_so_far, e2e cli.spec clicks the button

title: No other edits: every piece is a change
description: The review lists pieces no change holds as Other edits, folded after the flows (8l6.28, 8l6.42). There are none: every edit is a change. The review prompt asks for every piece in a change, a piece that fits none being a change of its own; the last request places each left piece into a change or makes new changes of them ('new', bound like the review's changes). A piece still no change holds (a failed or cut-short last request) is shown as a change of its own in docair's words, marked as such, in the card, the PR comment and the job's status; the store keeps them in 'other', so old stores show the same way.

Pieces still in 'other' show as changes of their own after the AI's: viewer review_view makes them (title from docair_words, recorded by docair, intro 'In docair's words...', no found off/check), the Other edits box is gone, the Changes button counts them; PR comment numbers them; serve status 'Reviewed: n changes in k requests' (project.rs). Tests: tests/page.rs lone-piece review, explain comment test, project.rs status; e2e fake-ai settle answers 'new', changes.spec checks 2 changes and the cart's code in change 2, cli.spec status. Docs: EXPLAIN 9.2/9.4/9.5/9.6/9.7 table, SPEC, GLOSSARY 'other edit' removed.

title: Found off: tell clear contradictions from what nothing mentions, and from risks
description: Found off mixes three things under one heading: claims the code contradicts (source commit/doc/comment), behaviour nothing mentions (source none), and mistakes or risks the AI sees (also none, shown as 'Nothing: no commit, doc or comment mentions it'). On docair's own review all three items were risks labelled as unmentioned. Each item gets a kind: contradicts (a commit, doc or comment says what the code clearly does otherwise, or a doc left out of date), unsaid (the code does something nothing mentions), risk (a mistake, missed case or risk in the code). The prompt asks for clear contradictions only; docair keeps a contradiction only with what was said, else it is a risk, and drops the said side of the other two. The card and the PR comment group them under their own headings, contradictions first.
acceptance_criteria: Card and comment show the three kinds under their own headings; the stored off has kind; old stores without kind still render; tests/page.rs, explain tests, e2e changes/cli specs; docair check 0/0
notes: Built: FoundOff.kind (contradicts|unsaid|risk) with FoundOff::kind() for stores without it (said -> contradicts, else risk); read() takes the model's kind with aliases, a contradiction with nothing said becomes a risk and is logged, unsaid/risk keep no source. REVIEW_PROMPT asks for clear contradictions only. docair_core::review::OFF_KINDS holds the headings (Said, but the code does otherwise / Done, but said nowhere / Looks wrong or risky); the card (page_changes off_item, off-group sections, viewer.css) and the PR comment group by them. Tests: explain a_review_binds_to_pieces_in_its_own_words (kinds, demotion, old store), tests/page.rs review test (three groups in order, unsaid drops what was said); e2e fake-ai gives all three, changes.spec/cli.spec check groups. Docs: EXPLAIN 9.1/9.3/9.4/9.5/9.6, SPEC, GLOSSARY found off, meanings.toml re-settled (7db7898d).
close_reason: Found off has three kinds under their own headings, contradictions first; e2e 71/71, workspace tests, docair check 0/0; real model on the shop: commit and README as contradictions, the price rise as unsaid

title: Found off: each item says what was said, where, and what the code does
description: A 'Found off' item is one sentence, so it is not obvious what is off against what. Each item becomes a pair: what a commit message, a doc or a code comment says (and which one), or that nothing says it; and what the code seems to do. The card and the comment show the pair side by side.
notes: Built: explain.rs FoundOff {source commit|doc|comment|none, where, says, code}, FoundOff::read (a bare sentence = code, said nowhere; none says nothing; no code = left out), check_where (a commit by its subject, a doc by its path, a comment by its part id; else where dropped and said), said() for the comment's '- **Said:** … **The code:** …'. Prompt: off as what was said against what the code does; only an off names what was said. page_changes.rs off_item: <dl class=off-item data-source> Said / The code. GLOSSARY 'found off' + meanings.toml. Real model, shop: the commit and README.md each set against the empty audit function, the price rise said nowhere. docair c1364fd..work: 5 changes, 1 other edit; one made-up commit citation dropped.
close_reason: Built and tested: e2e 69/69, workspace tests, clippy, docair check 0/0; real model on the shop and on docair itself

title: Review: the AI's own reading, checked against the code, with what is off; no quotes, no citations
description: Reported by the user: the review's text holds placeholders that say where it is from, or cites them ('The commit and the docs say …', '(docair-8l6.43)', 'from commit:c1364fd, doc:docs/EXPLAIN.md', 'put here by docair'); wanted is the AI's own interpretation of all the data, verified, highlighting what was found to be off. Build: the prompt makes commit messages and docs claims to check against the code texts; the why in the model's own words, never quoting or naming a commit, doc, issue or ticket; a list 'off' (a claim the code does not bear out, code doing what nothing announced, a mistake, missed case or risk in the code, a doc left out of date), and 'nothing found off' said when empty; no sources asked or shown, the digest sends commits and docs without ids; the last request also puts the pieces no change holds into their change with the model's words, instead of docair's module rule and its placeholder. Store schema docair.explained/2: older reviews are asked again.

Tests: a_review_binds_to_pieces_in_its_own_words, the_last_request_merges_and_places, page.rs, e2e changes/cli with the fake AI's new branches; e2e 69/69. title: Review asked in parts repeats a change: one change comes back from each request
description: Found running the real model on c1364fd with the parts' whole texts (docair-8l6.46): the input took 2 requests, each answered on its own, and two of the five changes came back twice (the 'What and why' card; the flows before the other edits). docair-8l6.31 allowed a change to be split across parts; with texts it now happens on a normal commit. title: The review's AI gets every changed part's whole text, before and after, with its comments, and the files no part covers
description: Asked by the user: the AI should get a better picture by being sent all changes, not only that a part changed but the whole function and its comments, so it can interpret what an edit does. Until now (docair-8l6.29) code went as signatures and summaries, and the model could only say that a body changed (on the shop example it guessed what). Build: for each new, gone or changed part, its source range (doc block, comments, code) at A and at B, read from the commits (git show) or the working tree; each piece in the request carries its parts' texts; files that changed but hold no part (a stylesheet, a Dockerfile, a config) go as their changed lines; the prompt says to read the texts and say what each edit does. Cut so it fits the requests (docair-8l6.8): a part's text at 4,000 characters a version, a piece's at 20,000, files at 2,000 each and 10,000 together.
acceptance_criteria: The digest of a two-commit repository holds a changed function's whole text before and after with its comment, and a changed file with no part as its lines; Rust tests; the real model's review of a commit says what a code edit does.
close_reason: docair-core review::{part_text, part_texts, PartText}, Intent.code and Intent.files; docair-server commits::other_files and the texts read with git show or from the working tree; docair-ai explain: a piece carries 'source' {part: {before, after}} capped at 4,000 a version and 20,000 a piece, the digest 'files', the prompt says to read them. Tests: a_parts_text_holds_its_comments, the_intent_is_read_from_the_commits_and_the_docs (a function's text before and after, a stylesheet's lines), a_review_binds_to_pieces_and_sources (the digest carries both). Real model: on the shop it now says the cart costs 120 cents an item instead of 100, and that the commit does not say so.

title: Code: who makes, takes and holds a type is not derived; 226 of 227 discovered structs have no line
description:
Structs, enums, type aliases and TypeScript interfaces are discovered as parts, but nothing derives who uses them. docair-scip keeps only references to functions and methods (`docair_scip::callable`), so every reference to a type is dropped: `Cli::parse()` and `match cli.command` in `docair-cli.main`, a parameter `&Graph`, a field `blocks: &[RawBlock]`. Calls to a type's methods become lines; the type itself gets none.

On docair's own graph (.docair/docair.graph.json, 2026-11-19, built with the code index):

| Discovered | With no line |
|------------|--------------|
| struct | 226 of 227 |
| enum | 36 of 38 |
| type alias | 8 of 8 |
| TS interface | 5 of 5 |

Example: `docair-cli.cli` (`struct Cli`, crates/docair-cli/src/main.rs:22). `main` makes it with `Cli::parse()` and dispatches on its `command`. The graph shows a part that nothing uses.

What this does to the chat: asked what the part is and who uses it, the AI reads the source and says that main uses it, which contradicts the graph. It then proposes hand-written tags to fill the hole (`@out args: Cli to docair-cli.main`, then `@out command: Command to docair-cli.main`). Those tags repeat what the code says, against docair-7lz (docair derives what it can, the AI only explains). They also get the direction wrong: main makes Cli, and Cli sends nothing.

Design first, in docs/ADAPTERS.md, as a new section beside §5.4 (calls) and §5.6 (data between calls):
- Which uses count: makes (`T { … }`, `T::new()`, a derive's `T::parse()`), takes (a parameter type), returns, holds (a field), matches on or reads a field. They come from the index (type symbols such as `Cli#`), and without an index from the signatures and paths the syntax shows.
- How it shows without flooding Code (1548 lines today). Options: a line per use; the type folded into what lines carry (§5.6 data lines already name `T`); or a "made by / taken by / held by" list in the type's details. Measure each on docair's Code layer before choosing.
- TypeScript: interfaces and types, from scip-typescript, the same way.
- What the AI's digest says about a type part, so that a question about it is answered from the graph.
acceptance_criteria: docair-cli.cli shows that docair-cli.main makes it and reads its command; docair-cli.command shows that main matches on it. The only discovered types left with no use are those that nothing in the project refers to, and the notes give their number. The design section in ADAPTERS.md lands before the code, and SPEC follows. Golden graphs move with a reason. docair check . stays at 0 errors and 0 warnings. The Code layer's layout time is measured before and after.

title: Page: a held part's lines wait for the drop; a click on an open box only selects it; a downloaded page has no AI
description:

design: Options, to discuss before building: (1) a datum's slice holds the lines that carry it and their ends, and folds the rest into closed boxes, so it is small; (2) a slice is not scaled top-down (its boxes keep words at their size; the picture grows and the reader pans); (3) Follow opens at the datum's first step at a readable zoom (zoom x scale >= 0.8, as a picked part does, SPEC §3.5) instead of the whole picture. A measure for the test: the share of a slice's words that show at 8 px or more when Follow opens.
acceptance_criteria: On docair's page, Follow on data.graph, data.page and data.question opens with every word in view at 8 px or more on a 1,200 px canvas; a Rust test holds the slices' smallest drawn word size; e2e checks the opening zoom of Follow.
notes: Built as decided in docair-702.27. layout_input::options_for(pic): a slice (pic.slice set) is laid out with no budget (budget infinite, floor 1), a layer or a section as before. It is used by lay_out_with, by kept layouts (layout_store; the key includes the options) and by the CLI (slice --layout, --layout, the measure loop). (b) was already the page's behaviour: a datum's slice is a walk, and show() starts it at step 1 with the step camera clamped to 0.8 to 1.3 px per unit. Measured with docair slice <id> --svg: data.graph went from a smallest word of 3.2 units to 11 (now 2075 x 4783, 107 parts, 202 lines), data.page and data.question likewise; no word below 11 units. On docair's own page in Chromium (canvas 1,200 px), Follow on data.graph, data.page and data.question opens at step 1 at 1.3 px per unit, the smallest word in view at 14.3 px. Rust test: tests/page.rs a_slice_keeps_its_words_readable, with a generated box of 30 functions passing a datum: scale 1 everywhere in its slice, below 1 when laid out as a layer. Scanning docair itself took 13 s in a test, so not that. e2e: data.spec 'Follow opens at the datum's first step, at a size to read' (scale 0.8 to 1.3, every word in view 8 px or more). The shop's golden SVGs are unchanged, since its slices never shrank. SPEC §3.5 and SLICES.md §5.
close_reason: Slices are laid out without top-down shrinking (options_for, decision docair-702.27): on docair's page Follow on data.graph, data.page and data.question opens at step 1 at 1.3 px per unit, the smallest word in view 14.3 px on a 1,200 px canvas; Rust test a_slice_keeps_its_words_readable; e2e data.spec 'Follow opens at the datum's first step, at a size to read'; full e2e 64/64.

title: Web app: a click on code in the embedded page breaks the page; in a tab of its own it works
description: Reported: in the web app, where the page sits in the result view's frame (before the reader uses Open in a new tab), a click on code breaks the page. Not reproduced yet; which click exactly (a code span naming a part, the Code layer, a source file:line) is to be pinned down first. The frame is sandboxed without allow-same-origin (result-view.html); it loads the page by its address when the server keeps the upload (src), else as srcdoc. The page's links are fragments (#part/<id>, #layer/<key>, page_panels.rs href); page.js follows plain a[href] links natively and only code spans (.node-ref) through go(), which sets location.hash.
design: Suspects, to check in this order: (1) srcdoc: a fragment link resolves against the web app's address, not about:srcdoc, so the frame navigates to the web app instead of moving to the fragment; fix by following every #… link through go() (or a <base> in the page). (2) Something in the click path that a sandboxed frame forbids. Storage is ruled out: sessionStorage and localStorage are already guarded (page.js remember/recall, the conversation's window.name fallback).
acceptance_criteria: The click is reproduced in an e2e test that opens an upload in the web app and clicks it inside the frame, with src and with srcdoc; after the fix the page stays and shows what was clicked; the same click on the page in its own tab still works.
notes: Reproduced in Chromium with a host page over http whose sandboxed frame (the web app's sandbox flags) takes the shop page as srcdoc. The header's #layer/code link and a details link #part/orders-api both loaded the host app into the frame, so the docair page was gone. With src the same clicks worked. Cause: in a srcdoc document a fragment link resolves against the parent's address. Fix: page.js's document click handler follows every a[href^="#"] itself (preventDefault, location.hash = href), except ctrl or meta clicks; page.js is at 998 of 1,000 lines. Checked: in srcdoc and src frames the Code layer shows, the part link shows orders-api's details, Back returns to #part/orders.create, no page errors. e2e by the other session: generate.spec 'a click on a link in the framed page stays in the page (src)' and '(srcdoc)', both pass.
close_reason: In a srcdoc frame a fragment link loaded the web app into the frame; page.js now follows every #… link itself, so the page stays and shows what was clicked, framed by src or srcdoc and in its own tab; e2e generate.spec covers both frames.

title: Placement: compare with dagre phase by phase, and take over what lowers crossings
description: dagre 0.1.2 had 1 to 7 fewer crossings (lines drawn straight) on 14 of docair's 24 data, route, scenario and walkthrough slices, while leaving out lines to boxes and making pictures 2 to 5 times larger (LIBRARIES.md). Compare the phases (cycle breaking, ranking, initial order, crossing reduction, positions, nested boxes) on the routed lines, not straight ones: route dagre's placement with docair's router. Take over what lowers crossings without making pictures bigger or slower, measured on docair's slices and layers.
notes: Built (crates/docair-layout only; public types unchanged). Method: 45 docair pictures (24 data, route, flow and walkthrough slices, the 16 part slices with the most lines, 5 layers). dagre's placement and ours were both routed by docair's router (a scratch crate turned dagre's output into a Placement). A scratch bench kept a baseline. An Explore agent read dagre's phases. Findings: dagre lays a hub out as a comb (left to right, every callee in one rank, its own module's and others'), but its nested boxes overlap and it leaves out lines that end at a box. Taken over, in order of effect: (1) a part with many lines is as wide as they need (ceil(lines/2)×12+16 px across the layers' direction): 1205 → 583 crossings; (2) a line leaving a box before its first layer or after its last becomes a fixed node in a layer of its own, with bend points in the layers between (ELK's ports, as nodes); the pull stays too: → 552; (3) for pictures of up to 60 lines, both directions' placements are routed and the cheapest wins, if the other direction fits the canvas at least 0.8× as well: → 398; (4) dagre's weighted median positions and alternating tie-break (biasRight): → 332 crossings, 1621 bends, 36.2 Mpx² (from 34.1), 0.7 s for all 45. Tried and dropped: network simplex ranking (883 → 888, no gain; removed), keeping the last of equally good orders (worse), crossings weighted by line weight (no change). dagre with the same part sizes: 286 crossings, 1372 bends, 141 Mpx²; per picture dagre better on 12, worse on 10, same on 23. docair-core.declare.settle: 37 → 0 crossings, laid out as a comb with clean boxes. All of docair: 13855 crossings in all (was 20706; Code 19385 → 13440, 11.7 → 7.3 bends a line), 1023 pictures in 11.8 s. Docs: SPEC §3.5, SLICES.md §5 (a table of the steps), LIBRARIES.md. 11 tests in docair-layout; clippy clean.
close_reason: Routed crossings on 45 docair pictures 1205 → 332 and bends 2532 → 1621 (room for busy parts, exit nodes, direction by price, median positions, alternating ties); now about level with dagre at a quarter of its area, with clean nested boxes.

title: Step 3.1: docair-layout, a crate of its own: input, text in one monospace font, a box laid out in layers, boxes sized and placed top-down
description: A new crate crates/docair-layout with its own input model (parts with a box, a size and a name; lines with ends, words, priority) and no dependency on docair-core, so it can become a library of its own. Text width in one monospace font: characters times one advance, wide East Asian characters twice. Each box laid out on its own in layers (our own layered placement instead of ELK: cycles broken by priority, layers, fewer crossings, positions), then sized inside out (budget 800, floor 0.7, the room for the box's name) and placed, as viewer.js topdownLayout does. Both directions; the one that fits a reference canvas best wins.
notes: Built: crates/docair-layout (no docair dependency; serde behind a feature). text.rs: Monospace (advance 0.6 em), columns (wide East Asian characters count 2, combining marks 0), wrap. layered.rs: own layered placement of one box. Cycles are broken by a weighted greedy order (Eades, Lin and Smyth; weight 1 + ahead). Layers: the longest path, then weighted-median moves within bounds. Bend points for long lines. Crossings: barycentre sweeps from model order, counted with a Fenwick tree (Barth, Jünger and Mutzel); the best order is kept. Positions: weighted isotonic regression per layer, 10 passes. Room between layers for words. Groups with no lines between them are packed in rows at about 1.6:1. Spacing is ELK's ×1.6. topdown.rs: lines lifted to the box that holds both ends (own lines keep their words), boxes laid out inside out with budget 800, floor 0.7 and padding 28/10/10/10, then everything placed; both directions, the one that fits a 1440×960 canvas best wins (the second must fit 1.1× better). 8 unit tests. Word decisions in docs/meanings.toml: direction, part, placement, text (term = false). docair check 0/0.

title: Step 3.3: the ways: each box learns where its lines go, and the cheapest placement wins
description: Port TOPDOWN_WAYS (ports per line or per part and side, ports in order, parts in order) and the choice between placements: a small picture priced by its routed lines, a big one by its lines drawn straight (straightPrice). A way with a port per line is left out above 40 ports in one box.
notes: Built: the four ways in docair-layout/src/topdown.rs (WAYS: a port per line; ports in order; a port per line with parts in order; ports and parts in order). In the own layered placement a port is a pull: a part is pulled toward the place, across the layers, where its line leaves the box in the first placement (BoxGraph.pulls). The pull counts in the barycentre sweeps, in a 'misplaced' cost next to the crossings, and in the isotonic positions. 'Parts in order' sorts a box's parts by where their lines go. A way with a pull per line is left out above 40 pulls in one box. The cheapest placement wins by straight price (length plus 400 per crossing; the router will price small pictures in 3.4). Placement records way and price. On docair: Network 3→1 crossings, Apps 187→173, Code unchanged (31600, its graph grew); all 972 pictures in 92 ms, slices 0.7 ms at most. Slices against baselines (scratch scripts, crossings drawn straight): as good as ELK or better on 20 of 24 data, route, flow and walkthrough slices; dagre 0.1.2 (scratch crate) had 1 to 7 fewer crossings on 14 of 24 but leaves out lines that end at a box, has no budget, gives pictures 2 to 5 times larger and takes 3–149 ms. Decision recorded in LIBRARIES.md: own placement.

title: Step 1: the slice model in core, and docair slice <id>
description: Port the rules of dataTour and the walk projection (viewer.js) to core. A slice starts from a datum, a part, a walk or a route; its ends have stable names; only certain lines by default, one-of and could lines marked; docair check reports what a slice covers. docair slice <id> prints it as JSON. Golden tests on the fixtures and on docair itself. Design: docs/SLICES.md.
notes: Built 2026-11-18. crates/docair-core/src/slice.rs (new): seeds, find, slice, all, to_json. Data slices port dataTour's rules exactly (made, there, back, inside for at most 6 hops, stretches of their own); a could line never carries a datum on inside other lines. Route slices take the part's lines plus the way in, back along calls, routes and selections, at most 8 hops. Flow and walkthrough slices take their steps. Other parts take their lines across their border, one hop. Each slice has ends with stable flags, boxes with 'more', the data on its lines, and for data, covers {lines, reached, apart} and how (named or typed). Part seeds are only parts that hold no parts: a box's lines reach 215 parts (browser). CLI: docair slice [seed] [--all] [--root] [--lenient]; check --coverage prints coverage for each datum. Tests: golden slices of shop, answer, platform and apis (crates/docair-adapters/tests/golden/*.slices.json), plus a_datum_slice_follows_its_way_there_and_back. On docair's own graph (scratch comparison against viewer.js dataTour), 9 of 9 data take the same steps. Slices: 9 data, 7 routes, 7 flows, 1 walkthrough, 859 parts; a part's slice has 4 parts in the middle, 11 at p90, 49 at most; data 25 in the middle, 57 at most. SPEC: CLI table, new §3.7. SLICES.md: coverage goes to --coverage instead of a warning; choice 5 decided by the numbers. cargo test --workspace, clippy and rustfmt are clean; docair check 0/0. Not done: the browser still uses its own dataTour until step 5. A route's way in reaches the gateways only where the graph links a Service to the program (docair-4wk.26).

title: Step 4: drawing in Rust: SVG for each section and slice
description: Rust writes each picture as SVG: kinds and colours, light and dark through CSS variables, line words. Saved pictures in tests. Design: docs/SLICES.md.

title: The CLI's knowledge is the product; the HTML is a self-contained wrapper drawn by Rust
description:
Decided 2026-11-18, for the epics Slices, Changes and Explaining changes.

1. The knowledge is what the CLI builds, makes obvious and links: the graph, slices, changes and explanations, as data and JSON, tested in Rust.
2. All UI generation moves to Rust: what to draw, the layout and the drawing itself (SVG). The HTML the CLI writes is the result. It is self-contained and fully usable on its own: every view and filter is baked in, with only a thin script (pan and zoom, hover tips, search over a generated index, glossary popups, stepping through walks). The browser generates nothing.
3. The AI works through the CLI, without the HTML. In the HTML, the AI features talk to the CLI running as a web server (docair serve), which they need.
4. The web app only uploads and shows the HTML.
5. docair does everything it can do reliably. The AI only links and explains, and only for the parts that changed. Its findings go to a place docair.toml sets; the user decides whether to commit them.
6. The move to Rust happens inside the Slices epic, not in an epic of its own.

title: Viewer: a pick of a part only Code draws lays out all of Code first (13.7 s for ask.digest)
description:
On docair's own page (1440x960), the word digest's popup offers 'see ask.digest'. Clicking it takes 13.7 s before the camera arrives. docair-ai.ask.digest is a function. Only the Code layer draws it as a part of its own, so select() runs layerFor(), which picks Code, then showLayer('code') lays out all of Code: 385 parts and 631 lines.

Measured with headless Chromium on a page scanned 2026-11-18 (1188 nodes, 1591 edges):

| What | Time |
|---|---|
| pick ask.digest from Network or Apps (layer switch to Code) | 13.7 s |
| pick ask.digest again, already at Code | 0.45 s (camera only) |
| Apps with docair-ai.ask opened (drill) | 0.56 s, draws ask.digest |
| layerFor() itself | 1 ms |

Which box holds ask.digest at each layer: Overview: docair-lib. Apps: docair-ai. Infra, Network, Kubernetes: none.

Cause: SPEC §3.4 says a pick of a part the layer leaves out goes to the first layer that is about it. For a function, that layer is always Code, and Code is the most expensive layout on the page (docair-4wk.22).

How to tackle: open the boxes that hold the part on the layer the reader is on, as drill() does. When this layer draws no box that holds it, open them on Apps, which Code goes up to. Go to Code only when nothing else can show the part, or when the reader asks for it (a 'show it at Code' link in the details).
design: To decide in the step: which layer comes first when the current one has no box for the part (Apps, or the layer layerFor picks with its boxes opened). Whether a part that a box opened at Apps now shows keeps the breadcrumb (Apps › docair-ai › ask) so the reader can close it again. SPEC §3.4 'Selecting a part that the layer leaves out' changes with it.
acceptance_criteria: On docair's page at 1440x960, picking docair-ai.ask.digest from the word digest's popup, the tree or a link, starting at Apps or Network, shows the part readable in 1.5 s or less. The camera still frames it as SPEC §3.5 says. SPEC §3.4 says what a pick does when the layer leaves the part out. An e2e test picks a function from Apps and checks the layer, the opened box and the time.
notes: Built 2026-11-18. crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js: select() asks pickWay (@id docair-viewer.pick-way) how to show a part the picture leaves out or draws only as a closed box. It opens the part's own box on the current layer when the layer draws a box around it, else on Apps, else it goes to layerFor() as before. showWay() opens the box (unfolding folded boxes around it), sets the breadcrumb focus, and toasts 'Apps · inside ask'. enterLayer() is the reset showLayer() did. The old Code-only quiet-part branch is folded into this. Correction to the description: at Apps the old pick selected the closed box docair-ai (2 ms) and never showed the function; only Network, Infra and Kubernetes went to Code. Numbers on docair's page (1440x960): ask.digest at Network 14.1 s -> 0.57 s drawn, 1.0 s with the camera (Apps, docair-ai.ask opened); at Apps -> 0.06 s drawn, 0.48 s with the camera, zoom x sc 1.0. A Deployment picked at Infra opens its release box there (0.5 s). docs/SPEC.md §3.4: new paragraph and a before/now table. e2e/tests/layout.spec.ts (e2e.layout): 'a function picked at Apps comes with its box opened, details first' and 'a function the layer has no box for comes at Apps' (Infra -> Apps for the cart's function, Infra keeps the cluster's service, a closed box at Code opens there). Time is measured by script on docair's page, not in e2e (the fixtures are small).
close_reason: A pick of a part the layer leaves out, or draws only inside a closed box, opens the part's box on the current layer or on Apps, and goes to the layer about the part only when neither can show it. On docair's page, ask.digest picked at Network comes in 1.0 s instead of 14.1 s. SPEC §3.4 and e2e.layout cover it; e2e 59/59 pass.

title: Uploads: run no indexer, read no code index outside the upload
description: Reported by the viewer session while reading docair-server: run_scan scans an upload with the upload's own docair.toml. (1) [code] run_indexers = true made the server run rust-analyzer scip on the uploaded Cargo project when rust-analyzer is installed (local server, e2e): rust-analyzer runs build scripts and proc macros, so an upload could run code on the server. Confirmed by hand: an upload whose build.rs writes a file did write it. (2) [code] scip paths were joined to the root unchecked: ../.., an absolute path or /dev/zero made the server read or hang on files outside the upload.
acceptance_criteria: An upload with run_indexers = true and a build.rs runs nothing; scip paths outside the root, absolute, through a link or to a device are W113; the local CLI still runs rust-analyzer on the user's own code.
notes: Built: Options::untrusted (docair-core lib.rs): scan sets [code] run_indexers = false for it; docair-server run_scan passes untrusted: true; CLI callers use ..Options::default(). docair-core config::inside(root, rel): relative, canonicalized (links resolved) and still under the root, a regular file or folder; docair-lang-rust index_of reads scip only through it, else W113 'the code index X is no file inside the project'. Tests: docair-core config inside_tests::a_path_in_docair_toml_stays_inside_the_root; docair-server an_upload_runs_no_code_and_reads_nothing_outside (fails with 'the upload's build script ran' when untrusted is off). title: Upload: the page looks frozen while it uploads, scans and draws (stuck at 'Generating… 0%')
description: Uploading docair's own folder (286 files, 7.8 MB) to a local docair-server: the button shows 'Generating… 0%' for 8 s, then the result view appears with an empty frame for another 1.5 s while the viewer lays out its first layer. Nothing moves and nothing says what is happening. Causes: (1) Angular 22's provideHttpClient() uses fetch by default, and fetch reports no upload progress. app.config.ts says XHR, but withXhr() is missing, so the percentage never moves. (2) Nothing is shown while the server scans or while the response downloads. (3) The generated page tells its parent nothing until it is ready, and the viewer shows nothing while a long layout runs: about 1.5 s for docair's first layer, up to 11 s at Code. How to tackle: withXhr(). One progress line with a bar for each phase: reading the folder (drag and drop), uploading (percent, MB), docair reads the files (indeterminate, elapsed seconds), receiving the page (percent). The viewer posts docair:ready to the parent, and the result view covers the frame with 'Drawing the page…' until then. The viewer itself shows 'Drawing…' and yields a frame before a layout that is likely to take long.
acceptance_criteria: Uploading a folder shows each phase with its progress: percent and MB while uploading, elapsed seconds while docair reads the files, percent while the page arrives, and 'Drawing the page…' until the page is ready. Regenerating shows the same. An e2e test checks the phases with a delayed scan answer.
notes: Built. Web app (web/src/app): app.config.ts uses provideHttpClient(withXhr()); Angular 22's default is fetch, which reports no upload progress, so the old percentage never moved. New progress-line component (@id docair-web.progress): the step 'N of 4', a bar (filled for upload and download, moving for scan and draw), bytes and percent, seconds while waiting, and after 10 s 'big projects take a while'. app.ts tracks the phases from HttpEvents: upload (UploadProgress), scan (all bytes sent), download (ResponseHeader, DownloadProgress), then the result. The upload panel shows the line under Generate, plus 'Reading the folder · N files so far' while a dropped folder is walked. The result view shows the compact line in its bar while regenerating, and covers the frame with 'Drawing the page: <layer> · N parts, M lines · s' until the page posts docair:ready (30 s fallback after load). Viewer: renderNow says what it draws (drawing(), @id docair-viewer.drawing), posts docair:drawing to the parent and yields a paint first (nextPaint, with a 60 ms fallback for hidden pages). A note with a spinner shows in the middle of the canvas once a layout takes 250 ms (CSS delay; compositor-run, so it moves while the layout holds the thread). Inside the web app it is left to the app until ready. Boot posts docair:ready, or failed: true. Measured on docair's folder (286 files, 7.8 MB) at about 3 MB/s, throttled: upload 2.7 s with a moving percentage, server 0.3 s, page 5.7 MB in 2 s, drawing 1.4 s; before, it sat at 'Generating… 0%' throughout. The 8 s server wait seen before was rust-analyzer running on the upload, fixed by the adapters epic (docair-4wk.23). Tests: e2e generate.spec.ts 'each step of a generation shows how far it is' (shop plus a 600 kB note, CDP throttling, phases upload/scan/download/draw in order with their texts); levels.spec.ts 'the page says what it draws while it lays out'. e2e 55/55; docair check 0/0. Docs: SPEC §1 (viewer note) and new §1.3, web/README.md, docs/meanings.toml [progress].
close_reason: Every step of a generation now says where it is: upload percent and MB, docair's reading in seconds, the page coming back, and the page drawing itself until it is ready.

description: The AI's review of the bug fixes (docs/changes/906ed6f1d7eb..work.json) found three faults: (1) a review asked in parts kept room for the ids of the others' pieces but not for the sentence around them, so a request could pass MAX_CHARS by a few hundred characters, and a very long list had no cap; (2) a stale review left out a change whose pieces are gone, with what it found off, without saying so; (3) the check that keeps @in/@out/@calls off a type matched '@in ' with one space, so '@in\tx' or '@IN x' slipped through. title: docair serve: events it ignores hold back the rewrite, e.g. a build writing target

title: Chat: each reply's edits add to the waiting ones; three edits to one part wait at once and would write three blocks
description:
In a conversation, `ProjectSession::take_reply` (crates/docair-server/src/project.rs:163) adds each reply's edits to pending.json with `pending.changes.extend`. Nothing checks whether an edit for the same node is already waiting. The page's chat and `docair chat` both go through it.

Three questions in a row about `docair-cli.cli` (`struct Cli`, no block) left three edits to that one node waiting ("3 edits wait to apply"). Each had its own summary and tag:

| Reply | Summary proposed | Tag proposed |
|-------|------------------|--------------|
| 1 | The parsed command line of the `docair` tool: the subcommand and its flags, … | `@out args: Cli to docair-cli.main` |
| 2 | The parsed command line: which subcommand ran … and its flags. | `@out args: Cli to docair-cli.main` |
| 3 | … which `docair-cli.main` parses once and passes field by field as arguments … | `@out command: Command to docair-cli.main` |

The node has no block, so each edit resolves to `insert` (`edit::resolve`). `edit::patch` then applies them one by one at the same line, so Apply & regenerate would write three blocks above `struct Cli`. This comes from reading the code; it has not been reproduced.

Fix: an edit to a node that already has one waiting is merged into it, not added beside it. The newer summary wins, a tag is added only once, and a tag the newer reply removes goes. The chat says that the reply replaced the edit already waiting for that part.
acceptance_criteria: A Rust test in docair-server: two replies edit the same node, and one edit waits, with the newer summary and each tag once. Applying it writes one block. The chat's count of waiting edits says 1. An edit to another node is still added beside it.
notes: Built: docair-server project::merge_changes; take_reply merges a reply's edits into the waiting ones, one per part (newer summary and why win, tags added once, a removed tag drops a waiting addition or is removed; glossary text/section/file edits replace the waiting one of the same file) and returns the parts replaced; docair.patch now holds every waiting edit (what Apply writes); the page's reply HTML says 'This reply's edit of X replaced the one already waiting for it'; docair ask prints 'replaced'. Test: project::tests::edits_of_one_part_wait_as_one (one edit waits, newer summary, tags once, another part beside it, applied it writes one block). SPEC 10.6.
close_reason: One edit waits per part (project::merge_changes), the chat and CLI say a waiting edit was replaced, docair.patch holds all waiting edits; test edits_of_one_part_wait_as_one; e2e 71/71

title: Chat: with no code in its input, the AI guesses how a type is used, states the guess as fact, and writes flow tags that get it backwards
description:
The AI's input has no source code (`docair-ai.ask.digest`; test `the_digest_marks_undocumented_nodes_and_has_no_code`). It also has no symbol and no signature. `docair-cli.cli` reaches the model as kind `component`, name `Cli`, in `docair-cli`, at `crates/docair-cli/src/main.rs:22`, undocumented, with no edge. That the part is `struct Cli`, and that `main` makes it with `Cli::parse()`, is not in the input (docair-4wk.35).

What the replies did with that:
- **Guesses stated as facts.** The first edit's reason says the reading comes from the part's place beside `Command` and `main`. The second answer still opens with "It is used: `docair-cli.main` parses the command line into `Cli` …", while the chart shows no line. Nothing tells the reader which of the two is true. The prompt asks for guesses to be marked with "probably" (ask.rs:66).
- **Tags that misstate the flow.** `@out args: Cli to docair-cli.main` says that Cli hands data to main, but main makes Cli. A type is what lines carry; it does not send anything. The third reply changed it to `@out command: Command to docair-cli.main`, which is another guess.

Fix, in docair-ai:
- The digest says what kind of code item a part is (its symbol: `struct Cli`, `enum Command`, `fn main`). Once docair-4wk.35 lands, it also carries the uses the code shows.
- The prompt says that a type is carried by lines and is not their sender or taker.
- An answer says plainly when the graph holds no relation, and that a claim comes only from names.
- The repair step leaves out an `@in` or `@out` added to a part whose symbol is a struct, enum or type alias, and reports it as a problem.
acceptance_criteria: The digest carries each part's symbol. A Rust test: an @out added to a struct part is left out, with a problem the repair request names. With the configured model, 'why is Cli not used anywhere?' gets an answer that says the graph holds no relation for it (before docair-4wk.35), or names main's use from the graph (after it).
notes: Built: the digest carries each part's code item ('item': struct Cli, fn main) when its symbol starts with a code keyword, never code; prompt: a struct/enum/interface/type is data the lines carry, never @in/@out/@calls; say plainly when the graph holds no relation, never a guess from names as fact. check_draft drops @in/@out/@calls added to a struct/enum/type/interface/union part, says it in problems and the repair request; an edit left with nothing goes. Tests: ask::tests::a_type_gets_no_flow_tags, the_digest_marks_undocumented_nodes_and_has_no_code (item, no code). Real model: 'Why is docair-cli.cli not used anywhere?' answered that the graph shows no relation and that the rest is a guess from names (docair-4wk.35 not landed). SPEC 10.2.
close_reason: Digest carries each part's code item; a type never gets @in/@out/@calls (left out, repair names it); answers say when the graph holds no relation; tests a_type_gets_no_flow_tags; real model said the graph shows no relation for Cli

title: Chat: every answer that touches a part with no block proposes edits, even when the question asks for none
description:
The system prompt (crates/docair-ai/src/ask.rs:52) says: "For a node marked "undocumented", give a "summary" … and the tags that say how data flows." The digest marks every part that has no block as undocumented (ask.rs:109). On docair's own graph that is 1309 of 1725 parts.

In a chat about `docair-cli.cli`, all three replies proposed edits to its block. The questions only asked what the part is and how it is used. The rule above outweighs the prompt's own "Change only what the user says or what the graph clearly gets wrong" (ask.rs:33). Every answer that touches one of the 1309 parts queues an edit, and docair-cli.cli shows that these edits pile up and contradict each other.

Fix: the reply proposes edits only when the message asks for them ("document …", "this is wrong", "… is missing"). Otherwise the answer may say in one sentence that the part has no block and offer to document it.
acceptance_criteria: The prompt proposes edits only when the message asks for them. With the configured model, 'what is this?' about docair-cli.cli is answered with no edits, and 'document docair-cli.cli' gives one edit. docs/SPEC.md §10 says when a reply carries edits.
notes: Built: SYSTEM_PROMPT (ask.rs): changes only when the message asks for an edit; a question about what a part is or does gets none, also for undocumented parts, and may offer to document it; 'document' an undocumented node gives summary and flow tags. Real model (GLM-5.3-Flash): 'What is docair-cli.cli?' and 'Why is docair-cli.cli not used anywhere?' gave no edits; 'Document docair-cli.cli.' gave one edit (summary only). SPEC 10.6 says when a reply carries edits.
close_reason: Prompt: edits only when the message asks for one; real model: 'What is docair-cli.cli?' gave no edits, 'Document docair-cli.cli.' one; SPEC 10.6

title: Chat: a question asked with ✦ Ask about this chips does not show in the chat what it was about
description:
A reader puts things into a question with ✦ Ask about this (docair-5n2, docair-702.28): a part, a line, a datum, a term become chips above the question, and the question posts them as context refs. Once sent, the chat shows only the typed words. Reading the chat later, a question like 'what does this do?' does not say what 'this' was.

Where it is lost (page.js chat):
- send() calls ask(..., q): say({ role: 'user', text: q }) logs only the text; the refs from context() are not kept in the message.
- add() draws a user message as plain text, so nothing could show the refs either.
- state.history keeps { question, answer } only. The next questions send that history to /api/ask, and docair_ai::ask turns it into user messages without the context, so the model also loses what an earlier question pointed at.
- The chips stay above the question after sending (S.refs is not cleared), so it is not clear whether they belonged to the last question or go with the next one.

To do: a sent question keeps its refs and labels; its chat bubble shows them as chips (name, the thing's link, as in a reply); the kept log (sessionStorage) restores them; a history turn carries its refs, so the AI's input for a follow-up still says what the earlier question pointed at. Decide with the user whether the chips clear after a question is sent.
acceptance_criteria: A question sent with a part chip and a line chip shows both chips in its bubble, with their names, and they link to the part and the line; they are still there after a reload; a follow-up question's request carries the earlier turn's refs and the fake AI's input names them; e2e with the fake AI covers it.
notes: Built: page.js: a sent question keeps its chips ([ref,label]) in its log entry and draws them in its bubble (data-test=asked): a part opens it, a datum and a term open their panels, a line is selected when the picture draws it; kept in sessionStorage; the Ask-about chips leave the box above (decision docair-t2z), the selection chip stays; the history turn carries its refs. docair-ai Turn.context; ask::messages adds 'What the question points at' to each earlier turn from ask_context::about. page.js stays at 1050 lines (three lines folded). Tests: ask::tests::an_earlier_turn_keeps_what_it_pointed_at; e2e ask.spec 'Ask about this puts a part, a line and a datum into one question' extended (3 chips in the bubble, chips above cleared, line chip selects the line, part chip opens the part, kept after reload, follow-up input names the earlier refs). SPEC chat section.
close_reason: A sent question keeps its chips in its bubble (each opens its thing, kept across reloads), the history turn carries its refs to the model; decision docair-t2z; e2e ask.spec extended, test an_earlier_turn_keeps_what_it_pointed_at

title: Pictures: a line's words sit on other lines (57% on docair's page) and grow to six lines
description: Reported from the web view: the words on a line are sometimes not clear: they overlap other lines, and some are very big. Measured on docair's own page (214 layers and sections, 7,172 words): 4,072 word boxes (57%) sit on a piece of another line, and 17% wrap to three to six lines (signatures with their via, such as "config: Config · graph : Graph +1 · via docair-ai › docair-viewer"). docair-layout's word_spots prices another line by the area its 2-unit strip shares with the word box, so a word settles on lines rather than move; words_size wraps at 28 columns with no limit.
notes:
Built:
- docair-layout text.rs: WORDS_COLUMNS (28) and cut(text, width, lines), which wraps, keeps the lines and ends the last in …; test words_cut_to_two_lines_end_in_an_ellipsis.
- docair-viewer layout_input.rs line_words cuts a line's words, via included, to two lines (decision docair-702.34), so the sizing and the drawing agree; the whole words stay in the line's tip and details.
- word_spots.rs prices every other line a word box sits on at 60 (as 20 px² of a part), where it was priced by the area its 2-unit strip shared; spots along a piece every 10 units, up to 30 each way (was 20 and 15).
- pictures.css: a word's tag is opaque (was 0.92) with a 0.6 edge in --line, and bundle words weigh 500 (was 600).
Measured on docair's page (214 layers and sections, about 7,240 words), before → after:
- words on three to six lines: 494 → 0;
- words on another line: 55.4% → 54.2%;
- lines under a word on average: 1.88 → 1.72.
In dense pictures lines run in parallel tracks 8 px apart, so a 17-unit word covers its neighbours wherever it goes; the tag keeps it readable.
Golden SVGs reblessed: apis.apps, platform.infra and shop.code each moved one word box (the new pricing), no text or part moved. layout.wasm rebuilt. Workspace tests, clippy, docair check 0/0. SPEC §3.5.
Full e2e 69/69 with the cut and the pricing. Measured whether the price or the room limits it: with each other line under a word priced at 1,000,000, 47.4% of words still sit on another line (1.21 lines on average), because no spot on or beside their line is free of other lines in dense pictures (parallel tracks 8 px apart). The price stays 60, since a higher one only pushes words onto parts. The levers left are room (wider gaps where words do not fit) or fewer words at once (a line's words shown once zoomed in enough to read, or for the selected part's lines). That is the user's call, so this stays open.
Then the user's choice (docair-702.35): crowded words show once zoomed in enough to read, and always for the selected part's lines, a picked line and a walk's step. At the starting zoom 16.0% of the words shown sit on another line, where it was 54%. More room between rows was measured and left out (−1.2 points for +3% area). Golden SVGs reblessed: platform.infra and shop.overview each got one word marked crowded with data-z. page.js is at 1,000 lines. SPEC §3.5.
close_reason: A line's words keep at most two lines (494 → 0 longer ones on docair's page), stand on an opaque edged tag, avoid other lines where a spot is free, and where none is they wait until the zoom makes them readable: at the starting zoom 16% of the words shown sit on another line, 54% before. Room measured and left out (decision docair-702.36). Full e2e 69/69; docair check 0/0.

title: A dropped upload shows raw JSON in the frame and in a new tab
description: After a restart or deploy, an hour unused, or 8 newer uploads, GET /api/projects/<id>/ answers 404 with {"error":"this upload is no longer kept; upload the folder again"}. The web app's frame and Open in a new tab show that JSON as text. Either the page's GET answers a short HTML page that says so, or the web app falls back to the HTML it already has (srcdoc, no AI) and says the AI needs a new upload.

Test an_upload_is_kept_and_served_as_a_project checks both answers and CORS. SPEC §1.3.

title: Two docair-server pods again: a request for a kept upload reaches the pod that keeps it
description: Decision docair-702.31 runs one server pod because kept uploads live in one pod. To run two again, either a pod forwards /api/projects/<id>/ to the pod that keeps the id (the id names the pod, e.g. its IP from the downward API; the NetworkPolicy then admits server to server), or the uploads move to storage both pods share (a ReadWriteMany volume; kind's local-path has none). Design first, in docs/SLICES.md §8 or a doc of its own; then server.replicas back to 2 and the doc blocks in server-deployment.yaml.
notes:
Recommendation (not started): forwarding, not shared storage. The id the scan answers names the pod that keeps it (its pod IP from the downward API, e.g. <ip-hex>-<random>); a pod that gets /api/projects/<id>/ for another pod forwards the request there, with the body and CORS kept; the NetworkPolicy admits server to server on the server port. Hash routing in the web nginx cannot work, since the id is made by whichever pod took the scan. A ReadWriteMany volume needs a provisioner kind does not have. Needs a short design in SLICES §8 first.
Built: crates/docair-server/src/peers.rs (Peers from DOCAIR_POD_IP + DOCAIR_PEERS, pod_of, forward with ureq: only to addresses DOCAIR_PEERS resolves to, x-docair-forwarded stops loops, GET/POST with body, content-type and accept), Config.peers, KeptUploads::keep_as with the pod in the id (<addr hex>-<random>), kept_upload_answer forwards before answering gone. Chart: DOCAIR_POD_IP (fieldRef) in server-deployment.yaml, DOCAIR_PEERS in configmap.yaml, templates/server-peers-service.yaml (headless), NetworkPolicy server to server on 8080, values server.replicas 2. Infra adapter: a fieldRef/resourceFieldRef variable is set by nothing (was a workload value, W108 on docair). Tests: a_pod_forwards_an_upload_it_does_not_keep (two real servers: page and POST through the other pod, forged id 404, forwarded never again), an_id_names_its_pod, the_variables_objects_set; smoke-test.sh 2b (the kept page 6 times in a row). Docs: SLICES §8 design, SPEC §1.3, ADAPTERS env row, LIBRARIES ureq row. Left: deploy and smoke-test in kind (drops kept uploads; ask the user first).
close_reason: Verified in kind (deployed by the other session after a full e2e run, 69 of 69): two docair-server pods Running; infra/smoke-test.sh passes, including check 2b, the kept page answering 6 times in a row whichever pod gets it. Code, chart, tests and docs as in the notes.

title: Every thing the page can reference has a unique, stable id: lines, steps, diagnostics
description: Parts and data have node ids (unique), terms have their glossary keys. Lines do not: a graph edge is known by its place in graph.edges, which shifts when the graph changes, and a picture's line is data-id=<its index in that picture> (svg.rs), unique in one picture only. A walk's step and a diagnostic have no id either. docair-5n2 links a thing into the chat by its id, and a conversation outlives a rewrite of the page (Apply reloads it, the conversation is kept for the tab), so the id must be unique across the page and the same after the next scan.
design: Proposal, to settle: an edge's id from what it is, not where it stands: <from> -<kind>-> <to>, with its label when two edges share those, and #2, #3 only for true twins; a picture's line takes the ids of the edges it stands for (data-edges holds ids, not indexes). A step: <walk seed>/<n>. A diagnostic: <code>@<node id>. One resolver in core turns any id into the thing (core, so CLI, server and page agree).
acceptance_criteria: graph.json gives every edge an id; no two are equal on docair, shop and platform (Rust test); an id survives a scan after an unrelated edit (test); the SVG and the panels use the ids; docair check stays at 0/0; golden graphs re-blessed with the reason.
notes:
Core side (this session): crates/docair-core/src/model.rs Edge.id; crates/docair-core/src/ids.rs edge_ids (from -kind-> to, the label when two share it, #n for twins; called in scan after word_and_prune), find(graph, id) -> IdTarget (Part, Line, Step seed/n, Diagnostic code@node #n, Term term:id), diagnostic_id. Test every_line_has_a_unique_stable_id (unique on shop, platform, apis, fold, answer, words; find gives each line back; an unrelated part added to the shop keeps every id). docair: 2491 lines, 2491 ids. Goldens re-blessed: every edge carries id. SPEC graph schema. Left for the other session: svg.rs data-edges and the panels use ids; 5n2 refs edge:<id>.
Page side (docair-viewer): svg.rs writes each line's data-edges as the ids of the graph lines it stands for, separated by 
 (svg::edge_key, which falls back to the index for a graph made without ids); the panels' line tips are keyed by id; page.js splits on newlines and a line's chip sends edge:<id> per line. tests/page.rs checks every edge's tip by id; the golden SVGs are reblessed for the ids alone (part, line and box counts unchanged); the svg test's colour check now looks for hex colours, not any #. Full e2e 64/64.
close_reason: Every line has a unique, stable id; steps and diagnostics resolve by id; the SVG and the panels use the ids.

title: Chat: reference parts, lines, data and terms from anywhere on the page in a question
description: Today a question to the AI takes one thing along: the selected part (page.js context(), POST /api/ask 'context': one part id, docair_ai::ask context: Option<&str>). The chat links to things (a reply's part names go to #part/<id>), but not the other way: a thing on the page cannot be put into the chat, and the reader cannot point at a line, a datum, a term, a step or a diagnostic, or at more than one part.
design: Decided with the user: next to each reference on the page sits an @ button; it puts the thing into the question by its unique id (@<id>, ids from the blocking issue), at the cursor. The chat knows the references: it shows each @<id> as a chip with the thing's name and popup, a typed @<id> works the same, and an id that names nothing is marked and not sent. The question goes with its list of ids to /api/ask (context: [id], the selected part as today unless cleared); the server resolves each id and the AI's input holds its facts. Open: which places get the button (panel links, tree rows, the details' header, a line's tip; in the picture only the selected thing, so the picture stays clean). Touches page.js, page_ai.rs, docair-server (/api/ask, openapi.yaml), docair-ai (ask), SPEC §10, SLICES.md §8.
acceptance_criteria: The @ next to two parts and a line puts three chips into one question; the request carries their three ids; the fake AI's input holds the facts of all three; a typed @<id> becomes a chip, an unknown one is marked and not sent; e2e with the fake AI covers it.
notes:
Server and AI side (this session): crates/docair-ai/src/context.rs about(graph, refs) -> (words, problems): part:/data: (id, kind, name, the summary's first line), term: (term or alias, any case; its summary), line:<k>@<address> (the picture at layer/, box/ or slice/, its line k's members), edges:<i>,<j>; a bare id is a part; refs naming nothing are named in problems. ask() sends them as '(What the question points at: …)'. crates/docair-server/src/lib.rs AskContext (one id or a list, untagged), ask_about joins the problems into the reply. openapi.yaml, SPEC §10.5. Tests: context::tests::each_ref_becomes_words_and_unknown_ones_are_named; e2e ask.spec 'a question points at parts, data, terms and lines'. Full e2e 59 passed. Page side: the other session.
Page side, as built: '✦ Ask about this' links. The CLI writes them in a part's details (part:<id>, page_panels.rs), a datum's page (data:<id>) and a term's entry (term:<term>, page_glossary.rs); page.js adds one to a line's details (edges:<i>,<j>). A click adds the ref to the chat's context chips (page.js context(); x removes one; the selected part is the first chip) and the question posts context: [refs]. Chips live until reload, so no index outlives a rescan. Checked in Chromium against docair serve with the fake AI: a part, a line (2 edges) and a datum reach the model as facts. tests/page.rs checks the links and the context area. The open chat takes its own column on wide screens (page.css; chat.css had width 100%). Not built against the acceptance: the @ button that puts @<id> at the cursor; a typed @<id> becoming a chip; an unknown one marked and not sent; e2e for the page side. Open: keep the Ask-about-this chips, or build the @ form.
Decision docair-702.28: chips, not @<id> in the question. Since docair-svh, a line's chip sends one edge:<id> per graph line it stands for. svg.rs data-edges holds the ids, separated by 
, and the panels' line tips are keyed by id. ask_context (other session) resolves edge:<id> through ids::find. Checked in Chromium against docair serve with the fake AI: part:orders.create, two edge:… refs and data:data.order reach the model as facts. Golden SVGs reblessed for the ids alone. e2e: ask.spec '✦ Ask about this puts a part, a line and a datum into one question'.
close_reason: Built as decided in docair-702.28: ✦ Ask about this in a part's details, a line's details, a datum's page and a term's entry puts each into the question as a chip, sent as typed refs (part:, edge:<id>, data:, term:); the model gets their facts; e2e ask.spec '✦ Ask about this puts a part, a line and a datum into one question'. Typed @<id> was not built (see the decision).

title: Legend: every kind is a coloured square; it does not say what the shapes and line styles mean
description: The legend (page_panels.rs legend) draws each kind as the same square swatch with a glyph. The picture draws kinds in shapes (svg.rs shape_of: api, tag for endpoint and config, rhomboid topic, hexagon workload, octagon job, concave hexagon gateway, ellipse network) and uses dashed outlines (external, unresolved, tests none or skipped, namespace and network boxes), lighter outlines for discovered parts, thicker lines for bundles, dashed lines (could, dangling, route, select, create), dotted lines (emit, consume, cover) and data chips. The reader cannot tell what a form stands for.
design: The legend draws each swatch with svg.rs's own shape and the picture's CSS, so the two cannot drift; a second group explains outlines and line styles, only those the project's pictures use.
acceptance_criteria: Each kind in the legend has the shape the picture draws; dashed and light outlines, line thickness, dashed and dotted lines and chips are explained; a Rust test checks the legend uses shape_of for every kind.
notes: Built: svg.rs kind_swatch/line_swatch/chip_swatch draw the legend's marks with the pictures' own outline() and classes: each kind in its shape_of shape and colours, each line kind in its style; 'What the forms say' explains dashed outlines (outside, unresolved, tests without result), a passed test, a closed box's double outline, a bundle's thickness, could and dangling lines, and data chips. Test: svg.rs the_legend_draws_each_kind_in_its_shape (every kind's swatch uses shape_of's element); tests/page.rs checks the legend's parts. The picture draws no lighter outline for discovered parts, so the legend does not name one.
close_reason: Done: the legend draws kinds and lines as the pictures do and says what the forms mean.

title: Page: move parts by hand, and their lines follow
description: The generated page cannot move a part: since the CLI draws the pictures, parts are not moved by hand (SLICES.md §10, the levels tests that went; SPEC §3.5 'A part moved by hand is not kept'). The reader needs to drag a part (and a box with what it holds) to make room or untangle lines. The old viewer did it with incremental routing (SPEC §3.5, 'moved by hand'); the router now lives in Rust and the page has none (page.js, budget 1,000 lines).
design: Open, to discuss before building: (1) what moves: a part, a box with its contents, several at once; (2) how the lines follow: straight while held and routed on drop, docair's router in the page (WASM), or a round trip to docair serve; (3) whether a move is kept: only for the tab, or as a layout hint the CLI reads (a patch of docair.toml, as docair-702.12), so the CLI stays the one documentation (docair-7lz).
acceptance_criteria: A part dragged on the canvas stands where it is put down; its lines end on its border at right angles and cross no part; a click still selects and does not move; e2e covers a move. SPEC §3.5 and SLICES.md say what is kept.
notes:
Decided with the user on 2026-11-18: docair-layout's router as WASM in the page. Layout side (this session): crates/docair-layout/src/draw.rs (num, rounded, arrow_length, line -> DrawnLine{d, arrow}: what svg.rs writes, moved out so svg.rs and the module share it), crates/docair-layout/src/hand_move.rs move_part(input, layout, PartMove{part, dx, dy}, width) -> MoveOutcome{parts, lines, layout}: the part and what it holds shift, the boxes around it grow (never shrink), the lines touching it are routed again around every part and their words placed again; test a_moved_part_takes_its_lines_and_its_box_grows. crates/docair-layout-wasm: answer(json) and the wasm exports alloc, free, move_part_json; layout.wasm (245 kB, 88 kB gzipped) kept with layout.wasm.version, scripts/build-layout-wasm.sh, profile.wasm in the root Cargo.toml; tests the_kept_module_is_built_from_this_code, a_request_is_answered_with_lines_ready_to_draw. Called from Node as the page will: 7 ms on a small picture. SLICES §7, ARCHITECTURE. Page side: the other session.
Page side (docair-viewer): page.js movePart (docair-viewer.doc-page.move-part). A part, or a box with what it holds, is dragged in the picture: while held it moves by a translate; on drop the router (IX.router, layout.wasm deflated) gets {input, layout, part, dx, dy, widths} from the picture's moves blob (IX.moves + i) and the answer is set in place: parts, boxes (rect, .bn, .tf-mark), lines (d, arrow) and their words. A move lasts until reload; a click without a drag selects. doc_page.rs packs one moves blob per picture, then the router last. tests/page.rs checks that order, each blob's input and layout, and that the router unpacks to \0asm. serde_json float_roundtrip in docair-viewer: kept layouts read back one ULP off before, and the moves blobs made a page from kept layouts differ (LIBRARIES.md). layout.wasm rebuilt (lib.rs had changed after the build). e2e: levels.spec.ts 'lines follow a part that is moved' (orders-db dragged 80x60 px: it stands there, its line ends on its border at right angles and crosses no part; a click moves nothing). Its steps pass in Chromium against docair serve; the e2e suite has not run it yet. SPEC §3.5 page bullets, SLICES.md test table.
e2e: the full suite passed 60 of 60, 'lines follow a part that is moved' included (393 ms). An earlier run of the same tree had one flake: ask.spec 'an uploaded page asks the server that keeps it', where the frame reloaded during an evaluate after Apply.
close_reason: A part or a box dragged in the page stands where it is put down; docair's router as WebAssembly routes its lines again in the browser, at right angles, ending on its border and crossing no part; a click still selects. e2e levels 'lines follow a part that is moved' passes; SPEC §3.5 and SLICES.md say a move lasts until reload.

title: Page: the data marked in a line's words (question, graph) look clickable, but a click does nothing
description: svg.rs marks the data a line carries in its words (rect.chip behind a tspan.d), so words like question and graph stand out in the picture. They carry no datum id, and page.js skips data chips inside #pic on click (wirePopups: d && !d.closest('#pic')). The reader expects them to work like the data chips in the panels.
design: svg.rs writes the datum's id on each chip (data-data), so the page can treat it as a .data-ref: hover shows the datum's popup, a click opens its details page with Follow. The click must not also select the line under it (or selects both, decided with docair-nts).
acceptance_criteria: Hovering a marked word in the picture shows the datum's popup; clicking it opens the datum's details; a Rust test checks the id on the chip; e2e covers the click.
notes: Built: svg.rs carried() keeps each data word's datum; chips_in returns the datum per match; a line's words write rect.chip[data-data] and tspan.d[data-data]. page.js: hovering one shows the datum's popup (and not the line's tip), a click opens the datum's page. Golden SVGs reblessed: only data-data added on the chips (7 files). Checked in Chromium on the shop's Apps picture.
close_reason: Done: data in a picture's line words carry their datum; hover shows its popup, a click its page.

title: Page: a click on a line selects it and shows its details
description: A line in the picture has a tip on hover (the first 8 graph lines it stands for), but a click on it, or on its words, does nothing: the pointerup handler in page.js only looks for .part and .box. The reader needs to click a line to see what it is.
design: Like a part: the line gets .sel, its two ends are lit; the details panel shows the line as the CLI wrote it (packed like the part details): every graph line it stands for, its ends and the parts it passes as links, the data it carries as chips, the walks it is in. Open: an address #line/<id> for the back button and links.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a line or its words selects it and fills the details panel; Escape or a click on the canvas clears it; the camera stays; e2e on the shop covers it.
notes: Built: page.js pickLine(): a click on a line or on its words (not a datum in them) selects the line (.line.sel, accent, 3 px) and shows its two ends as links and the graph lines it stands for (the CLI's edge tips) in #details [data-test=line-details], under a walk's card when one plays. Checked in Chromium on the shop: orders-api → orders-db.
close_reason: Done: a click on a line selects it and shows its details.

title: Decision: the walk's call-stack order is tested in Rust

The logic is docair-core slice::messages now, so the test moved to crates/docair-adapters/tests/fixtures.rs (a_call_stays_open_while_its_callee_works_in_later_steps), with the same two cases; e2e checks the step cards.

title: Decision: parts hidden by [view] hide are left out of every picture
description: As SLICES.md §4 says, the CLI applies [view] hide: the parts are in no picture, the page shows no chip, and the reader cannot show them again in the page (the old page started with them hidden and offered a chip). [view] show brings a part back inside a hidden section, also in the CLI. To revisit: whether the page should offer them, which needs pictures drawn with them too.

title: Decision: test lines show how many tests, not their words

This is how viewer.js drew test lines. Seen while porting ask.spec (Word the lines). To revisit: draw a single test line's own words.
