title: Decision: #part/<id> goes to the part's home, not into the reader's layer
description: A part the picture on screen draws stays where it is; any other goes to its home: its box's section, else a layer (Apps first), else its slice (docair-viewer.doc_page.homes). The old page opened the part's box on the reader's layer, or went to Apps, with a toast (Apps · inside Cart). e2e/tests/layout.spec.ts tests the new rule. Hidden chips use the box's label as the picture does (infra host).
notes: Settled with the user on 2026-11-18: #part/<id> keeps going to the part's home (one fixed address per part), and the page says where it went in a short note (in orders-api · Apps).
close_reason: Settled with the user; the follow-up is its related task.

title: Decision: docair serve does not aim at a quick re-layout after file changes
description: Decided with the user on 2026-11-18: docair computes on command. The router keeps 5 rounds. Measured on docair's Code layer (563 parts, 1,232 lines, under load): 1 round 2.6 s (+38% crossings), 2 rounds 5.3 s (+17%), 3 rounds 8.1 s (+9%), 5 rounds 13.4 s. docair serve still writes the documentation again when files change; whether it should only do that on a command is open.
notes: Settled with the user on 2026-11-18: a new docair build is the on-demand path (scan and write the documentation, nothing served); docair serve keeps watching the project's files, with a better mechanism than looking every second (OS file events, debounced, ignoring outputs and build folders). Follow-up: see the task linked here.
close_reason: Settled with the user; the follow-up is its related task.

title: Decision: a view change waits as a patch of docair.toml
description: In docair serve, a reply's view change (hide or show) is no longer applied to the page at once: it waits with the edits, ServeAnswer.patch holds docair.toml as it will be written (unified diff), Review shows it, POST /api/apply writes it and the documentation is written again. Built in crates/docair-server/src/project.rs (view_text, answered), test a_view_change_comes_as_a_patch_of_docair_toml. The old web app hid the section at once and offered Undo.
notes: Settled with the user on 2026-11-18: a view change from the chat only hides in the page, as the reader's hiding; it never writes docair.toml. The CLI's docair ask --apply keeps writing [view] (an explicit command).
close_reason: Settled with the user; the follow-up is its related task.

title: Decision: an uploaded page has no AI, for now
description: Decided with the user on 2026-11-18. The web app only uploads and shows the page docair wrote; docair-server scans an upload in a folder it throws away, so there is no project to ask about or to apply edits to. The AI is in the page docair serve serves (docair-702.6.3) and in the terminal (docair ask, docair chat). To revisit: docair-server could keep an upload as a project for a while and tell the page where to ask (sessions, cleanup, CORS for the frame). Docs: SLICES.md §8, SPEC §1.3.
notes: Superseded the same day: the user asked to integrate the AI, and uploads now keep it (docair-702.6.7: the server keeps each upload as a project).
close_reason: Superseded: the AI works in uploaded pages (docair-702.6.7).

title: Keep the code index (SCIP) per hash of the files it reads, so a scan after an edit is quick
description: docair scan . on docair takes 6.0 s, 5.5 s of it rust-analyzer's SCIP index. Once the CLI writes every picture (docair-702) and docair serve writes the documentation again after an answer or an applied edit (docair-702.6), that scan is what the reader waits for. ADAPTERS.md §11 plans a cache per file hash for later: keep the index under a hash of the files it reads, and run the indexer only when they changed.
notes: Built: crates/docair-scip/src/lib.rs, with rust_analyzer_version, rust_index_key (FNV-1a of the version, every .rs and Cargo.toml file by path and text in path order, and Cargo.lock), cache_dir ($DOCAIR_CACHE, $XDG_CACHE_HOME/docair, ~/.cache/docair) and kept_rust_index (written as .part, then renamed; the six newest are kept). docair-lang-rust index_of uses it instead of a temporary file. On docair: docair check 7.24 s cold, 0.66 s warm; after an edit 7.56 s (the indexer runs); with the edit undone 0.68 s (the first index again). Unit test: the key ignores file order and changes with a file, the indexer's version or the lock. SPEC §1.1 and ADAPTERS.md §11. Files that docair.toml excludes but rust-analyzer reads are not in the key.
close_reason: The Rust code index is kept under a hash of what rust-analyzer reads: a scan of unchanged code 7.2 s → 0.7 s on docair.

title: Step 6: the HTML shows explanations and workflows
description: The HTML shows the stored explanations and workflows, and asks more through docair serve. Draft design: docs/EXPLAIN.md.
notes:
Confirmed by the user on 2026-11-19, as laid out: docair build --changes <A> adds a #changes section (each changed flow: new, gone or changed, the parts it now goes through or no longer does, moves apart, A and B pictures side by side drawn by docair, uncertain flows marked); stored findings from docs/changes/<A>..<B>.json show per flow (explanation, workflow before and after steppable like a walk, the model's links), and a served page can ask docair serve to explain flows without findings. Page side: the other session; the build flag and POST /api/explain: this session.
Server side wired (this session): POST /api/explain {a, b?} -> ChangeFindings (crates/docair-server/src/project.rs explain), on the served project and the upload router; stores findings like docair explain; 409 for a root without git (kept uploads), 503 when AI is off. Tests: explaining_needs_commits_to_compare (Rust), e2e cli.spec docair explain also POSTs to docair serve on the two-commit repo (helpers.ts serveFolder). SPEC §10.5, openapi.yaml.
docair serve --changes <A> (this session): ProjectSession.changes; write_outputs renders through docair_server::commits::changes_page (compare_work with the server graph as B, findings from findings_file), falls back to the plain page when A cannot be read. POST /api/explain without b compares against the server graph, and with --changes rewrites the page and bumps the version. Changes.working_tree (core) tells the page to leave b out. Tests: a_page_without_commits_has_no_changes_section; e2e cli.spec docair explain serves with --changes HEAD~1, explains the working tree, sees the version bump and the explanation in #details at #changes/flow:checkout. SPEC, CHANGES §5.
Page side (docair-viewer page_changes.rs). The stored findings (ChangeFindings as JSON, through Changed.findings) show in each flow's details: the explanation (code spans become <code>, linked to their parts by the glossary linker, terms marked), who recorded it and when (or 'corrected by hand'), and the workflow's '▶ before · n steps' and '▶ after · n steps'. Each side of a workflow is a still picture of that version's slice at #changes/<seed>/before and /after, walked through like any walk: its steps, packed with the walks, light the parts they are in (or the box that holds them), frame them, and the card says what the user does. The list shows the model's links (a at A is b at B: why) and 'n of m not explained yet' with the command (docair explain A [B]). Served (docair serve --changes, the other session's), a '✦ Explain them' button POSTs /api/explain {a, b only when !working_tree} and reloads (page.js 1,000 lines, room made in wire and movePart). Checked in Chromium against docair serve --changes HEAD~1 on two commits of the shop with the fake model: 2 of 2 unexplained, Explain, reload, explanation shown. Tests: tests/page.rs an_explained_change_shows_its_finding_and_workflow; e2e changes.spec "an explained flow shows the model's words and walks its workflow". SPEC §3.5, EXPLAIN.md §5.
close_reason: Stored findings show in the changes section: the explanation and who recorded it, the workflow walked through before and after, the model's links, the flows not explained yet with the command, and an Explain button under docair serve --changes. Page test an_explained_change_shows_its_finding_and_workflow; e2e changes.spec 'an explained flow shows the model's words and walks its workflow'; full e2e 69/69.

title: Step 7: tests with the fake AI, and the cost limit

title: Step 3: explaining what each change does to its flow
description: For each changed flow, the AI says what the change does, recorded with the model and the time. Draft design: docs/EXPLAIN.md.
notes: Built: explain.rs bind(): an explanation only of a flow that changed and naming in backticks only ids of A or B (parts or lines), else the whole explanation is left out and the unknown ids named; FlowExplained with recorded.

title: Step 4: workflows from the user's side, before and after

The prompt asks for the user side and to leave it out when the flow is nothing a user does (decision: it starts where the flow starts, docair-8l6.10).

title: Step 5: the store, docair explain <A> <B>, and a PR comment
description: A docair.toml key says where the findings go; the user decides whether to commit them. docair explain <A> <B> works without the HTML; in a pipeline it writes Markdown for a PR comment. Draft design: docs/EXPLAIN.md.
notes: Built: [explain] store and max_requests (docair-core config ExplainSettings); crates/docair-cli/src/diff.rs compare() (shared with docair diff) and cmd_explain: findings in <store>/<short A>..<short B or work>.json (docair.explained/0), a flow already there (a human correction above all) not asked again, explain::comment() for a pull request comment (one line per changed flow, the explanation under it, workflows and links in <details>). SPEC CLI table and docair.toml, EXPLAIN.md.
close_reason: The store, docair explain, and the pull request comment.

title: Explaining changes: the AI links and explains, and shows how the changes affect the user
description: The AI gets only the changed slices from Changes (docair-zrr), never the whole graph. It links what docair cannot prove is the same (a part renamed with a changed body, an old flow and the new one) and explains what each change does to its flow, with workflows from the user's side before and after. Every claim is bound against the graph. The findings go to a place docair.toml sets; committed, they carry over, and in a pipeline they become a PR comment and are dropped. docair explain <A> <B> works without the HTML; the HTML shows the findings and asks more through docair serve. Draft design: docs/EXPLAIN.md, to be discussed and updated once Slices (docair-702) is done (see docair-zrr.1).
acceptance_criteria: On the two-commit fixture, docair explain links and explains each changed flow with the fake AI, every claim binds against both graphs, a link that does not bind is dropped with a warning, and the PR comment is written; the AI's input stays under its size limit.
notes:
2026-11-18: draft spec docs/EXPLAIN.md written; to be discussed and updated in docair-zrr.1 once docair-702 is done.
2026-11-19: the review is reworked with the user (steps 10-17, docair-8l6.17 to .24; decisions .25 to .30). The unit of review becomes a change, one difference in what the app does, made understandable by the AI from docair's pieces, the commit messages and the changed prose; docair binds every claim and covers every changed piece; flows become context. Version 0 needs the AI; the number of changes is not capped. Step 10 writes the design into EXPLAIN.md §9 first.

title: Step 1: the AI's input: a digest of the changed slices only
description: A digest of the changed slices from Changes, with a size limit; digest in crates/docair-ai/src/ask.rs sends every part of the graph today. Draft design: docs/EXPLAIN.md.
notes: Built: crates/docair-ai/src/explain.rs digest(changes, a, b, flows, with_unlinked): per changed flow its seed, how, certain, its changed, added and removed parts in a few words (id, kind, name, first summary line, signature) from the graph they are in, its line ids added and removed; the first request also the parts removed at A and added at B. Never the whole graph (e2e checks the request names no Terraform part of the shop). Requests are cut at MAX_CHARS 60000, flow by flow.
close_reason: The AI's input is the changed flows only, with a size limit.

title: Step 5: changed parts and the slices through them, compared at A and B
description: The changed parts: the graph diff joined with the changed lines matched to parts, config files included. The slices through them at A and B, compared by their stable ends, on certain lines only, with a mark when a change rests on a could line. JSON out (read by Explaining changes) and a short Markdown summary. Draft design: docs/CHANGES.md.
notes: Built: crates/docair-core/src/changes.rs changes(a, b, graph diff, changed lines, names): changed parts = added, removed, changed, moved, and the smallest part each changed line (git diff -U0, changed_lines) falls in at A or B; every non-part slice (scenario, walkthrough, datum, route) through one is compared by seed: parts and line ids at B (A ids rewritten for moves), how = changed / new / gone, certain unless a changed line is one-of or could. JSON docair.changes/0 (changes.json), markdown(). Test a_unified_diff_gives_the_changed_lines_of_each_file.
close_reason: Changed parts and the slices through them, compared; JSON and Markdown.

title: Step 6: the changes section in the HTML
description: The HTML shows each changed slice at A and at B side by side, with the positions of the parts that stayed kept. Draft design: docs/CHANGES.md.
notes:
Confirmed by the user on 2026-11-19, as laid out: docair build --changes <A> adds a #changes section (each changed flow: new, gone or changed, the parts it now goes through or no longer does, moves apart, A and B pictures side by side drawn by docair, uncertain flows marked); stored findings from docs/changes/<A>..<B>.json show per flow (explanation, workflow before and after steppable like a walk, the model's links), and a served page can ask docair serve to explain flows without findings. Page side: the other session; the build flag and POST /api/explain: this session.
CLI side wired (this session): docair build --changes <A> (crates/docair-cli/src/main.rs cmd_scan) compares the working tree with A through docair_server::commits::compare (moved there from the CLI so the server shares it), reads stored findings from [explain] store/<key>.json, and calls docair_viewer::doc_page::render_page_with with Changed {before, changes, findings}; also writes .docair/changes.json. On docair, --changes HEAD: 6 changed flows. SPEC CLI table.
Page side (docair-viewer):
- doc_page::render_page_with(graph, keep, Option<&Changed{before, changes, findings}>), the entry point for `docair build --changes <A>` and `docair serve --changes <A>` (the other session wired both); render_page_keeping calls it with none.
- page_changes.rs builds the header's 'Δ Changes · n' and the list: each changed flow with new, gone or changed, '+ parts / − parts', uncertain ones marked; the reading-changed warning; the moves apart.
- Each flow opens at #changes/<seed>: one still picture (IX still: nothing in it is moved by hand), drawn from the slice at A and at B side by side under 'Before · A' and 'After · B'. svg::draw_marked with ChangeMarks marks ch-added parts and lines at B and ch-removed at A. A side the flow is missing from says so. The flow's details show with it (P.flowChanges).
- The pictures are packed after the others, each with an empty moves blob; page.js: the button opens the list, a change picture shows its flow's details, and a still picture's parts are not dragged (page.js 1,000 lines).
- Not done: keeping the stayed parts' positions between A and B (CHANGES.md §5); each side is laid out on its own.
Tests: tests/page.rs a_changed_flow_shows_before_and_after; e2e changes.spec 'a changed flow is listed and drawn before and after' (two commits of the shop, docair build --changes HEAD~1). On docair, `docair build . --changes HEAD` shows 29 changed flows. SPEC §3.5, CHANGES.md §5.
close_reason: The changes section is in the page: Δ Changes · n, the list of changed flows (uncertain marked, moves apart), and each flow before and after side by side at #changes/<seed>, gains and losses marked. Page test a_changed_flow_shows_before_and_after; e2e changes.spec 'a changed flow is listed and drawn before and after'; full e2e 69/69; docair check 0/0.

title: Step 7: tests on a fixture repository with two commits
description: A fixture repository with two commits: a rename, a new step in a flow, a rerouted request, a changed Helm value. docair diff reports each as expected. Draft design: docs/CHANGES.md.
notes: Built: crates/docair-cli/src/diff.rs test two_commits_give_their_flow_changes: a git repository made in the test, commit A and B: total renamed sum with the same body (a move, the flow unchanged by it), tax body changed, a new step save in the buy scenario (flow:buy changed, now through shop.save); graphs kept in the cache. Also fixtures.rs two_graphs_differ_in_moves_changes_and_new_parts. A rerouted request and a changed Helm value are not in this fixture (decision issue).
close_reason: The two-commit shop runs through docair diff (cli.spec) and through the page: changes.spec 'a changed flow is listed and drawn before and after' builds it with --changes HEAD~1 and finds the checkout before and after, the audit step marked; full e2e 69/69.

title: Step 1: parts know where they end
description: An end line on SourceRef (crates/docair-core/src/model.rs has a file and a first line only), filled in by every adapter, so changed lines can be matched to the parts they fall in. The golden graphs move, with the reason given. Draft design: docs/CHANGES.md.
notes: Built: SourceRef.end (model.rs; serde: absent when unknown); facts Symbol.end, Hints.end (merge copies it); build sets a node source end from its symbol, else its block end_line. Rust adapter: the item end row; TypeScript: the declaration and statement ends. Infra parts discovered without a block have no end (decision issue). Goldens re-blessed: node sources carry end (orders.create 1 to 11, orders.list 13 to 20, shop-ui.cart 1 to 24). SPEC graph schema, CHANGES §3. Workspace tests pass.
close_reason: Parts know where they end, from the adapters or their blocks.

title: Step 2: a fingerprint of each part's body
description: A fingerprint of each part's code, so a part moved or renamed with the same body is linked to itself between two commits. Draft design: docs/CHANGES.md.
notes: Built: crates/docair-core/src/diff.rs fingerprint(text, node, names): the code from the part first line to its end (SourceRef.end), the doc block above it skipped, comments and spacing left out, every part name of the graph replaced, punctuation kept; fingerprints(graph, read) for a whole graph, from the files of that commit. Test a_body_keeps_its_fingerprint_when_renamed_or_moved. Computed when diffing, not stored in the graph (decision issue).
close_reason: A fingerprint of each part's body, from its commit's files.

title: Step 3: the graph diff in core
description: The diff of two graphs: parts, lines and tags added, removed or changed; moves and renames linked by fingerprint. Golden tests on two graphs. Draft design: docs/CHANGES.md.
notes: Built: crates/docair-core/src/diff.rs diff(a, b, fa, fb) -> GraphDiff { reading, added, removed, changed (body, kind, name, summary, part_of, route, tags), moved (a part gone at A and new at B with the one same fingerprint), lines_added, lines_removed, lines_changed (carries, words, via, reach) }: parts by id, lines by id (docair-svh) after rewriting A ids for the moved parts, so a rename changes no line and its callers stay unchanged. Test two_graphs_differ_in_moves_changes_and_new_parts (fixtures.rs: load renamed read is a move, run unchanged, save body changed, extra added with its line).
close_reason: The graph diff in core, with moves by fingerprint.

title: Step 4: docair diff <A> <B> reads two commits
description: docair diff builds the graph at both commits and keeps a built graph for each commit. How commit A's files are read, whether uncommitted work can be B, and how slow code indexers stay affordable are decided in docs/CHANGES.md.
notes: Built: crates/docair-cli/src/diff.rs cmd_diff and graph_at: git rev-parse of A and B; each commit through a detached git worktree in a tempdir (removed after), scanned and fingerprinted, kept as graphs/<sha>-<docair version and docair.toml hash>.json in the cache folder; without B the working tree. SPEC CLI table. On docair HEAD vs the working tree: 9 s.
close_reason: docair diff reads two commits, keeping each commit's graph.

title: Changes: what two commits change in app structure and flows
description: docair diff <A> <B> says how the changes between two commits affect the app structure and the flows, not the text. A flow is named by its stable ends; the path between them is what changes, so a rename or move is no change in itself. The changed parts are what the graph diff shows changed plus the parts the changed lines fall in; the slices through them are compared at A and B. docair does all of this reliably, without the AI and without a browser; the HTML shows A and B side by side. Draft design: docs/CHANGES.md, to be discussed and updated once Slices (docair-702) is done.
acceptance_criteria: On a fixture repository with two commits, docair diff names each changed flow (a new step, a rerouted request, a changed Helm value) and reports a pure rename as no change; JSON and Markdown out; the HTML shows the changed slices at A and B with positions kept.
notes: 2026-11-18: draft spec docs/CHANGES.md written; to be discussed and updated in docair-zrr.1 once docair-702 is done.

title: Step 0: once Slices is done, discuss Changes and Explaining changes with the user and update their specs and steps
description: The specs docs/CHANGES.md and docs/EXPLAIN.md and the steps of both epics are drafts, written before Slices (docair-702) was built. When Slices is done, go through both epics with the user, update the docs and the steps, and only then start step 1.

Done without a meeting, as the user asked for decisions to be taken and recorded: docs/CHANGES.md and docs/EXPLAIN.md updated (no longer drafts; what epic 1 gives: line ids, slice seeds, the page draws any slice), their open questions decided (§7 of each) and recorded as decision issues under docair-zrr and docair-8l6. Steps unchanged in number; step 6 of Changes (the HTML section) is built in the page's files by the other session from this epic's JSON.

docair-zrr.2's block by this gate is now a related link: the specs are updated and the open points decided (the user asked to decide and record instead of meeting), so the steps proceed; this gate stays open until docair-702's decisions are reviewed.

title: Step 3: Apply & regenerate updates the open page in place
description: The app sends the new graph and the page's texts (docair-html, taken from the new page) into the open page (docair:graph) instead of loading a new page into the frame. Kept: the layer, zoom and pan, the selected part (cleared when it is gone), opened boxes, hidden sections, the tests switch, the walkthroughs replies added. boot() splits into what is done once (Cytoscape, the wiring, the workers) and what is done for each graph. docair writes the viewer's version into each page and the page says its own in docair:ready; when they differ, the app loads the new page as today. SPEC section 10.6. Design: docs/REGENERATE.md section 4.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: the frame is not loaded again; the layer, zoom and selection stay; a page updated in place equals a new page of the same graph; a page from another viewer version is loaded as a new page.
close_reason: Superseded by docair-7lz: the web app only uploads and shows the HTML. Not started.

title: Step 1: the layout key holds what the layout reads, and the layout code's version
description: Today's key (layoutKey in crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js) holds every field of the parts and lines, so edits that move nothing give a new key: a failed test (its name's ✓ becomes ✗) lays out Code again, and one new @calls renumbers the lines' members and lays out all six layers of docair's page. The new key: per part its id, parent, compound, w, h and minW, and the name of a box; per line its id, source, target and label; the hints; the canvas, direction and font; and a hash of the docair-app and docair-elk scripts (3 ms over 1.9 MB), since kept layouts will outlive their page. The worker gets the same input, made by the same function, so a layout cannot depend on a field the key leaves out. Design: docs/REGENERATE.md section 2.
acceptance_criteria: Pages made from docair with one change each: a description edit lays out no layer, one new @calls lays out apps and code only, a failed test lays out no layer. A test checks the keys of a fixture with these changes. The pictures are the same as before.
notes: Built, checked and reverted (2026-11-18). In crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js: layoutInput (parts: id, parent, compound, w, h, minW, a box's label; lines: id, source, target, label), layoutKey over that input plus a hash of the docair-elk and docair-app scripts (3 ms over 1.9 MB), the worker sent the same input. Same pictures on every layer of docair's page and of the shop, old against new viewer, in the workers and on the page thread. Keys on docair's page with one change each: a description line, no layer (none before); one new @calls, apps and code (all six before); a failed test, no layer (code before). e2e/tests/regenerate.spec.ts written; it failed against the old viewer, as designed. Reverted, since layout moves to Rust (docair-7lz, docair-702); the key's design carries over (docs/REGENERATE.md section 2).
close_reason: Superseded by docair-702: layout moves to Rust (docair-7lz). Built, checked and reverted; the key's design carries over (docs/REGENERATE.md section 2).

title: Step 2: kept layouts across pages: IndexedDB for a page on its own, the app's store in the web app
description: A layout is kept by its key beyond the page. A page on its own keeps it in IndexedDB (works in Chromium on file://, where pages from disk share one store; Code's 290 kB layout is written in 5.8 ms and read in 4.9 ms). In the web app the page's sandboxed frame has no storage (SecurityError), so the app keeps the layouts in its own IndexedDB: the page asks by key and hands over each new one by message, and the app marks the page it shows so that the first layer asks too. No size limit of its own: a write the browser refuses is skipped. The page checks a kept layout's shape before drawing it; the app takes messages from the frame only. SPEC section 3.5. Design: docs/REGENERATE.md section 3.
acceptance_criteria: e2e: a reloaded page draws Code without laying it out; Apply & regenerate after a description edit lays out nothing. On docair's page, Code is drawn from a kept layout in about 0.2 s instead of 11.8 s.
close_reason: Superseded by docair-702: the browser lays out nothing (docair-7lz), so it keeps no layouts. Not started.

title: Regenerate: only what changed is laid out again
description: A page that is made again or opened again keeps the layouts of the pictures that did not change, and Apply & regenerate in the web app updates the open page in place. Measured on docair's page: Code is laid out in 11.8 s every time a page opens; drawn from a kept layout it takes 0.19 s. Design: docs/REGENERATE.md (agreed 2026-11-18): the canvas counts exactly in the key, no size limit of its own, the update in place as step 3.
close_reason: Superseded by docair-702 (layout in Rust, docair-7lz). Not built; docs/REGENERATE.md sections 1 and 2 carry over to the Rust layout.

title: viewer.js is two parts: 227 functions under the docair-viewer crate, 31 documented ones under docair-viewer.page
description:
The dependency matrix prototype shows a cycle between docair-lib and docair-viewer.page, made of 74 call lines. All of them run between two halves of the same file, crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js. The TypeScript adapter files its undocumented functions under the docair-viewer crate as docair-viewer.assets.viewer.* (227 parts). The doc blocks put the documented functions under docair-viewer.page (31 parts), the page as it runs in the browser. So wireGraph, nodeLink and renderTree (crate) call select (page), and the page's functions call back into the crate's.

Expected: one file, one place. Code found in a file whose documented parts run somewhere else (here the page, @part-of docair-viewer.page under browser) goes with them. Otherwise the Apps and Code layers draw the viewer's script twice, and calls between its halves look like dependencies between a library and a program.

How to tackle: in merge (docair-core), place an undocumented symbol under the part that the documented blocks of the same file belong to, when they all agree. Or the adapter takes the file's @part-of from its first doc block. Check the golden graphs.
acceptance_criteria: On docair's page every function of viewer.js sits under docair-viewer.page. The matrix and the Code layer show no lines between docair-viewer and docair-viewer.page that run between two functions of viewer.js. The golden graphs are blessed with the reason.
close_reason: Obsolete since docair-702.5: viewer.js is gone.

title: Viewer: lay out a picture's placements in two layout workers side by side
description: Part of docair-4wk.22. The first Code layout of docair's page takes 14.2 s; ELK placements are about 5.8 s of it: the two directions (DOWN 1.0 s, RIGHT 0.8 s), then the ways from TOPDOWN_WAYS that suit the picture ('ports in order' 2.1 s, 'ports and parts in order' 1.9 s). Placements of one step don't depend on each other, so two workers can lay them out side by side: the directions at once, then the ways at once, each worker taking the next placement when it is free. The page chooses, as topdownPlace does now, and one worker routes the lines of the winner. The same picture; without workers the page lays out as before.
acceptance_criteria: On docair's page, Code's first layout is about 2 s faster with the same picture (layer script); the first view of the page is no slower; e2e passes, layout.spec included; without workers the page still lays out by itself.
notes: Built (crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js): LAYOUT.workers, two layout workers (LAYOUT_WORKERS, no more than hardwareConcurrency). The page coordinates (layoutThere): topdownFirst and topdownPlace now choose among placements laid out by a runner. On the page that is placeHere, one after another with a shared box cache; in the workers it is inWorkers, each worker taking the next placement when it is free. Then one worker routes the winner (routeLines, shared with computeLayout). Worker steps: 'place' (placeOne, placeSafely) and 'route'. A worker keeps the boxes laid out for the newest picture. LAYOUT.next still counts layouts (layout.spec). Measured with the layer script on docair's page (1293 nodes, 2057 edges, 1440x960): every layer the same picture; Code 14.2 s → 12.0 s; the page ready in 0.66 s instead of 1.05 s; Infrastructure 0.41 → 0.18 s, Kubernetes 0.56 → 0.28 s, Apps 0.29 → 0.18 s. Without workers (LAYOUT.off) the page draws the same Code picture. e2e 59/59, docair check 0/0. SPEC §3.5.
close_reason: The placements of a picture are laid out in two workers side by side: Code 14.2 s → 12.0 s and the page ready in 0.66 s, the same pictures.

title: Viewer: a pick that changes layer shows the part's details only after the layout
description:
select() in crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js sets S.selected and calls showLayer(key).then(() => select(id, center)). The details panel, the tree row and the #id in the URL change only once the new layer has been laid out. On docair's page, picking docair-ai.ask.digest from Apps leaves the old details on screen for 13.7 s, with nothing to say the click was taken.

How to tackle: render the details, mark the tree row and set the URL at once, then switch the layer and move the camera when the layout is done. A newer pick during the layout wins, as a newer layout run already does (S.layoutRun).
acceptance_criteria: After a pick that changes the layer, the details show the picked part within 100 ms, whatever the layout takes. A second pick during the layout ends on the second part. An e2e test checks the details before the layout is done.
notes: Built 2026-11-18. viewer.js: select() is now markSelected() (URL, tree row, details, docair:selected to the parent) right away, and onCanvas() (canvas selection, lit lines, camera) once the picture is drawn. A pick that needs a new picture waits for it in showWay(). A pick made while any layout is under way waits for drawn() (new: S.shownRun, the newest run drawn). Each continuation checks S.selected, so a newer pick wins. Boot awaits a #id pick before docair:ready. On docair's page the details show within 50 ms of the pick at Network (the layout then takes 0.57 s). Picking ask.digest and then docair-core.build 30 ms later ends on build: details, canvas selection and both boxes opened (file:// and HTTP). e2e.layout checks that the details show in the same task as select() while the layout is still pending.
close_reason: The details, tree row and URL change as soon as a part is picked, and the canvas follows once its picture is drawn; a newer pick during a layout wins. Covered by e2e.layout; e2e 59/59 pass.

title: Viewer: lay out off the main thread; the page freezes for a long layout
description:
The viewer inlines elk.bundled.js, which runs ELK in a fake worker on the main thread. docair's router (gridLines) runs there too. While Code lays out on docair's page (13.7 s at 1440x960), the page paints 47 frames, and the longest gap is 1.6 s. Hovering, panning, scrolling and the layer buttons wait until the layout is done.

Where the time goes (CPU profile of one Code layout):

| Part | Time |
|---|---|
| ELK, 24 calls over 6 placements (2 directions + 4 TOPDOWN_WAYS) | 7.5 s, longest call 1.6 s |
| gridLines (search 4.0 s, roughWay 1.6 s) | 5.7 s |
| everything else (Cytoscape, labels, boxes) | under 0.5 s |

How to tackle: run ELK in a real Worker, made from a Blob of the inlined ELK worker script (elkjs takes workerUrl or workerFactory). Move gridLines into the same worker if its inputs can be passed as plain data. Check that it works from file://, inside the web app's iframe, and under the page's CSP (worker-src). A newer layout run can then terminate the older one instead of waiting for it.
acceptance_criteria: During a Code layout on docair's page, no frame gap is longer than 100 ms, and a click on another layer stops the layout and draws that layer. The page works the same from file://, from docair serve and inside the web app. Layout results are the same as on the main thread (the layer script's crossings and detours do not change).
notes: Built 2026-11-18. viewer.html: the ELK and viewer script tags have ids (docair-elk, docair-app). viewer.js: the layout worker (@id docair-viewer.layout-worker) is a Blob of the ELK source plus the viewer source, wrapped in a function so 'use strict' holds. In the worker the script only calls serveLayouts() (no boot). That takes self.onmessage back from ELK's own worker code, and ELK runs there with its fake worker. computeLayout() is the old layoutFor body, made pure: flow hints go across as data (hintsData/hintsFrom), and fitZoom/topdownFirst/topdownPlace read the canvas size and direction from a ctx argument instead of S. measure() uses an OffscreenCanvas in the worker. layoutJob() shares the job under way for the same key. A newer picture terminates the worker (stopLayout) and the next job starts a fresh one. If the worker fails to start or breaks, workerFailed() lays out on the page from then on, the job under way too. firstLayer() uses the worker as well, and stops when the reader picks a layer first. The drag reroute stays on the page. Numbers on docair's page (1440x960, 1977 edges): during the 23 s Code layout the longest frame gap is 20 ms with no long tasks (was a 6.1 s task, gaps up to 1.6 s). Clicking Apps 1.5 s into a Code layout draws Apps 0.78 s later. Worker vs page on the same picture: network 493/499 ms, apps 603/650, k8s 567/609, code 23.1/23.6 s, and identical positions and routes on all four. Works from file://, over plain HTTP, and in a srcdoc iframe with the web app's sandbox (Chromium). e2e.layout 'the worker lays out inside the web app too'. The drawing note and the docair:drawing and docair:ready messages are unchanged. SPEC §1 and §3.5 'Beside the page, and once'.
close_reason: ELK and docair's router run in a worker built from the page's own scripts: during docair's 23 s Code layout no frame waits longer than 20 ms, a click on another layer stops the layout and draws that layer in 0.8 s, and the picture is identical to one laid out on the page. Falls back to the page without a worker. e2e 59/59 pass.

title: Viewer: keep each layer's layout; going back to a layer lays it out again (Code 13.4 s each time)
description:
Every showLayer() runs a full layout, even for a layer that was laid out a moment ago with the same parts. On docair's page (1440x960): Apps → Code 13.8 s, back to Apps 1.2 s, Code again 13.4 s.

How to tackle: keep the result of layoutFor() (positions, routes, labels, scales, direction) per picture. The key is what visibleElements() returns: the ids, parents and sizes of the parts, the lines, and the direction and canvas size the placement was chosen for. renderNow() takes a kept result instead of laying out again. A moved part (drag reroute) updates the kept routes. Keep a few pictures, not all: the Code layer of docair's page is the large one.

Related: docair-4wk.22 also proposes reusing placements between a layer and a walk's view of it; the same store can serve both.

title: Viewer: a part picked from a link must come close enough to read, and stand out
description:
Picking a part from outside the canvas selects it and moves the camera to it. Afterwards the part is often too small to read and too faint to spot: the reader cannot tell at a glance which box it is, or where in the picture it sits.

Where a pick comes from (each calls select(id, true) in crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js):

| From | Function |
|------|----------|
| a part's name in the details | nodeLink |
| a row in the tree | renderTree |
| a diagnostic | renderDiagButton |
| a chip in a walk's step card | stepCard |
| "Read more" and "Show it" in a word's popup; a part named in an explanation | termMore, wireTerms |
| `#id` in the page's URL | the page's start |

Why (select, @id docair-viewer.show-details): the camera centres on the part at zoom max(current zoom, 1).

- It ignores how small the part is drawn. The layout draws what is inside a box smaller (node data `sc`, font size `fs`), so at zoom 1 a function inside a module inside a program has a few pixels of text.
- It does not fit the part: a large box at zoom 1 can run off the canvas.
- The mark is weak: a selected node gets a 3 px accent border, the same as a search hit (node.hit). Nothing draws the eye once the camera stops.
- A part on another layer, or in a closed box, is laid out again first (showLayer, render); the camera then starts from wherever the new layout put it.

The walk camera already solves the readable part: cameraFor and frameStep take `sc` into account, and never frame a step below zoom 0.8 in drawn size (SPEC §10.4, "never smaller than readable").

A click on the canvas itself does not move the camera, and should stay so.
design:
To decide in the step:

- Frame the picked part with cameraFor: the whole part on the canvas, its label readable (zoom × sc ≥ TOUR_MIN_ZOOM), and room around it, so its box and neighbours show where it is.
- Mark it: for example a short pulse or halo once the camera arrives, and a selected style that differs from a search hit.
- Maybe say where it is in words too: the boxes around it, as the zoom-in breadcrumb does (Apps › docair-lib › docair-core).
acceptance_criteria: After a pick from a link, the tree, a diagnostic, a step chip, a word's popup or the URL: the part is fully on the canvas, its label is readable (zoom × its draw scale ≥ 0.8, as for a walk's step), and the box around it is in view when that still fits at a readable zoom. The picked part stands out at a glance, and looks different from a search hit. A click on the canvas still does not move the camera. An e2e test picks a nested part by a link and checks the zoom and that the part is on screen. SPEC §3.4 or §3.5 says what a pick does to the camera.
notes:
Built 2026-11-18:
- crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js. The viewer session owns this file and applied the change as a patch. select() calls showPicked when a part is picked outside the canvas. New, next to cameraFor: showPicked (@id docair-viewer.show-picked), pickCamera and pulse. The camera puts the part in the middle at zoom × sc = 1, never below 0.8. The part's box stays in view when it fits at a readable zoom. A part too large to read whole is shown whole. A reader who is closer already keeps their zoom. node:selected has a halo (underlay in --accent, opacity 0.3, padding 8 × sc). It swells twice when the camera stops, except with reduced motion. .dim, .flow-dim and .carry-dim skip the selected part.
- docs/SPEC.md §3.5: new paragraph "Pick a part", with a before/now table.
- e2e/tests/pick.spec.ts (e2e.pick, 2 tests). First: a part picked by a link ends in the middle, readable, fully on the canvas, not dimmed by the search, with a halo that a search hit lacks. Second: a click on the canvas does not move the camera. The first test fails on the old viewer, where the search dimmed the picked part to 0.16.

Numbers on docair's own page (canvas 830 × 870):
| Picked | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| docair-core.build at Code | zoom × sc 0.49, words 5.9 px | 1.0, words 12 px |
| docair-server at Code | zoom 1, a box 1381 px wide, off the canvas | zoom 0.51, all in view |
| docair-server.scan_upload at Network | 0.84 | 0.85, its release box in view |

Validation: e2e 53/53 passed (results.json); docair check . has 0 errors and 0 warnings.
close_reason: A pick from a link, the tree, a diagnostic, a step chip, a word's popup or #id brings the part to the middle at its designed size (zoom × scale 1, never below 0.8), keeps its box in view when that fits, and shows a too-large part whole. A halo that pulses twice marks it, and the search, walks and data never dim it. A canvas click leaves the camera alone. Covered by e2e/tests/pick.spec.ts (passing) and SPEC §3.5.

title: Following data: the walk misses data that travels back as a reply (5 of 8 data items reach none of their lines)
description:
SPEC §3.6: Follow walks where a datum is made, then every line that carries it, in the order it travels, and those lines stay lit. On docair's own page this fails for most data. Following ◇ digest gives one step ('ask.digest makes digest') and leaves out the one line that carries it (docair-ai.ask.ask -> docair-ai.client.chat). Of the 8 data items with lines, 5 reach none of them (page 0 of 6, digest 0/1, reply 0/16, walkthrough 0/4, patch 0/5) and 3 reach some (question 7/12, files 15/18, graph 7/36).
Cause: dataTour() in crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js only walks along the arrows from the part that makes the datum. A call line carries its payload along the arrow and its reply against it, and a function that makes a datum usually returns it to its caller (ask.digest returns the digest to ask.ask, which sends it on to the model). Neither a reply nor that return is followed.
How to tackle: (1) Know which side of a line carries the datum: the payload (along the arrow) or the reply (back). The core already finds carries by matching payload and reply words (edge.carries); have it record the side (for example carries and carries_back), or let the viewer match the datum's words against payload and reply. (2) In dataTour, let the datum travel back along a line that carries it in its reply, and from its maker back to the callers of the maker. (3) Lines that carry it but that the walk cannot reach still go into the walk, at the end, so none is left out silently.

title: Following data: the walk plays on Apps, where its parts and lines sit inside one box
description:
Every data walk on docair's page plays at the Apps layer. A datum mostly travels between functions inside one crate, which Apps draws as one closed box: following ◇ digest marks the whole docair-ai box as the step, and the line that carries the digest is not drawn at all, because both its ends are inside that box. The reader has to find 'Open ▸ this step inside docair-ai' to see anything.
How to tackle: choose a data walk's layer by where its lines are drawn as lines: count, per layer, the carrying lines drawn between two parts against those folded into one box, so a datum that moves inside one crate plays at Code. Or keep the layer and open the boxes its steps are in, as walks already open modules at Code (walkView). Do this after the reply fix (docair-nkm), which gives the walk the lines to count.

notes: Built (viewer, crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js): dataLayer(base) picks a datum's layer: the one that draws most of the walk's lines as lines between two parts, not folded into one box; on a tie, fewer steps that only Open shows, then the higher layer. defaultLayer uses it for data walks; openStep gives an opened data step the datum's messages. Second cause, fixed: classify's leaf rule closed docair-ai at Code, because its direct parts (modules) are only found in the code, while the functions inside them have doc blocks. A box now stands closed only when nothing inside it has a doc block ('told' set). On docair's page (1552 edges), every data walk plays at Code with 0 steps that need Open: digest 3 steps, 2/2 lines drawn; reply 32 steps, 33/33; walkthrough 10, 9/9; patch 8, 7/12 (the rest are network hops Code leaves out). At Apps before: reply 11/33 lines drawn with 14 of 17 steps hidden in a box, patch 2/12, question 4/23. The fold fix adds 31 parts and 41 lines at Code. e2e 53/53 (data.spec covers the walks at Code); docair check 0/0. SPEC §3.4 Code row (fold rule), §10 walk layer (data walks). Cost: the first step of a data walk at Code waits for the Code layout: reply 5.7 s, patch 3.6 s, question 5.3 s on docair's page. Filed as docair-4wk.22.

title: Meanings: the page explains every word from what the project defines, code first
description:
Looking at facts on docair's page, it was not clear what a fact is, although the project defines it: the module doc of crates/docair-core/src/facts.rs ('Facts: what adapters learn from the code. Adapters report facts and never touch the graph...'), docs/ADAPTERS.md §4, docs/IMPORTS.md §2. The viewer explains only GLOSSARY.md terms (SPEC §13.2), so nothing else docair knows reaches the reader. Even the glossary's own 'adapter' entry says 'reports facts' and leaves the word unexplained.

Goal: every word a reader may not know is explained on the page, from the best source the project has, and deciding what a word means is done once and kept.

Sources docair already reads that define words:
1. Doc blocks and native docs (//!, ///; docair-4wk.4) of the symbol that implements a word: docair-core.facts, Symbol ('Something that exists in the code'), Evidence, Inferred, Draw.
2. Doc headings that name a concept ('## 4. Facts: the contract between adapters and core').
3. GLOSSARY.md entries, the place for words with no code of their own (Ingress, Helm, Terraform).

The design doc is docs/MEANINGS.md (step 1); SPEC §13 follows it.
design:
Decisions (2026-11-17):
• Source code is the best source, always. A word's definition comes first from the doc block or native doc of the symbol that implements it, then from GLOSSARY.md, then from doc headings (docs/MEANINGS.md §2).
• The glossary is checked against the code. Where an entry contradicts the code's definition, the code wins and the contradiction is reported.
• The AI may expand a definition or word it better, starting from the code's.
• Where a word is not clear (a term or an ordinary word; which of two definitions applies; whether a summary defines the word or only names a node), the AI decides. Each decision is recorded in the repository, so it is a one-off effort per word: the next run does not ask again.
• docair check warns about a word the texts use but nothing defines and no decision covers.
• docair glossary and '✦ Explain the terms' build entries from the definitions the project already has, code first, instead of writing new ones from nothing.
• The hover says where an explanation comes from (the node, the doc section, the glossary); Read more opens it.

Open for docs/MEANINGS.md:
• Where and in what format decisions are recorded: in GLOSSARY.md itself (an entry whose See: names the code, a list of words that are not terms) or in a file of their own.
• How a changed source reopens a decision (a digest of the defining text).
• How a contradiction is found (the AI, since it is about meaning), how it is kept, and how check and the page show it.
• How common node names (check, build, scan, merge) are kept from underlining every text.
• The new warning codes.
acceptance_criteria: On docair's own page, hovering 'facts' shows what a fact is from facts.rs, names the source, and Read more opens it. A second explain run on an unchanged tree asks the AI nothing new. docair check warns about an undefined word on a fixture and stays at 0 errors, 0 warnings on docair. SPEC §13 says where the page's explanations come from.

title: Imports: OpenAPI and AsyncAPI descriptions
design:
- Adapter crate docair-lang-apis, registered in docair_adapters::all() (ADAPTERS.md §5.1, §5.3).
- Facts: the description is a symbol (new kind `api`). Each operation is a declared Http meet with payload, reply, operationId and evidence (file:line). AsyncAPI channels are declared Topic meets with send/receive and the message name.
- Core: a declared meet never counts as a server, so a handler and its description are not "two servers of one route". It is matched with the code's Serve at the same meet. Requests that meet it take payload and reply from it when their block says nothing. Unserved operations become endpoint nodes inside the description's node, which goes into the package or service that owns its directory and disappears when nothing is left in it.
- YAML and JSON with line numbers: serde-saphyr if it gives spans (LIBRARIES.md chose it for the rules), else saphyr 0.3.3 (checked: YAML and JSON, a line per key and per parse error).
- Diagnostic codes are picked when implemented, after docair-4wk.6 has taken its own.

title: Import decisions: declared routes in the facts model, and five more
description:
Decisions before Import 1.

1. How facts say "this description declares a route" without serving it. Otherwise a handler plus its description are two servers of one route. Options: (a) a role on Serve: implements | describes; (b) a new fact Declare { at: Meet, payload, reply, name, evidence }. Recommended: (b), so Serve keeps meaning "this code runs here". It touches the facts model docair-4wk.2 is building now.
2. A description is its own node (kind `api`) inside its service, removed when everything in it merged. Recommended: yes.
3. Operations without a handler are drawn as endpoints (plus a warning). Recommended: yes.
4. Inside an external part, only the operations the code calls are kept, so a vendored description with hundreds of operations stays small. Recommended: yes.
5. YAML crate: serde-saphyr if it gives line numbers, else saphyr 0.3.3.
6. Dogfooding: a hand-written crates/docair-server/openapi.yaml, checked against the routes from code. Recommended: yes.
acceptance_criteria: Each choice recorded in this issue's notes; the facts-model change agreed with docair-4wk.2.

Serve now has at: Meet (Meet::Http only so far), so Declare { by, at: Meet, payload, reply, name, evidence } fits beside it. docair-58a adds Declare, Meet::Topic and the api kind in crates/docair-core/src/facts.rs; merge ignores declares until docair-58a.3.

title: Import 1: read API description files into facts
description:
New crate docair-lang-apis (LanguageAdapter), registered in docair-adapters.

- Finds descriptions: YAML by its first key (openapi, swagger, asyncapi), sniffed without parsing, so Helm templates are never parsed; JSON by name, via [import] apis (defaults **/*openapi*.json, **/*swagger*.json, **/*asyncapi*.json) and a json row in the language registry with no comment syntax, so package-lock.json and the like stay unread.
- Emits the description symbol and one declared Http meet per operation: method; base + path; payload (the body's $ref name, Order[] for arrays, else the parameter names); reply (the first 2xx schema); operationId; evidence file:line.
- Base path: the path of servers[0].url ({var} defaults, relative URLs, none = /); path-level and operation-level servers override it; 2.0 basePath; [[import.api]] base wins.
- Versions 2.0, 3.0, 3.1; 3.2 like 3.1 without the query method and additionalOperations.
- A file that can't be parsed gets the parse-failure diagnostic (ADAPTERS.md §9.4); the scan goes on.
design:
docair.toml:

[import]
apis = ["contracts/*.json"]     # more JSON files to read, besides the defaults

[[import.api]]
file    = "api/openapi.yaml"
part_of = "orders-api"          # the service it describes
base    = "/api"                # instead of the servers' path
ignore  = ["GET /healthz"]      # routes left out on purpose

Core: facts.rs Declare/Role/Meet::Topic and Facts.declares; check.rs kind api; lang.rs json row (Family::Data); discover.rs reads JSON only when named like a description or listed; config.rs [import] apis and [[import.api]] file/part_of/base/ignore; adapter.rs Project.config. title: Import 2: descriptions meet the code
description:
Core: declared meets meet the code.

- A declared Http meet is matched with the code's Serve at the same meet (the path algebra from docair-4wk.6; parameter names ignored; base path optional). The serving symbol gets the operation's summary and description as docs.
- Requests that meet it take payload and reply from it when their block says nothing; the evidence is the description ("from openapi.yaml").
- A declared meet never counts as a second server (no ambiguity warning).
- Operations nobody serves become endpoint nodes inside the description's node (kind api).
- Placement of the description node: [[import.api]] part_of, else x-docair-part-of in the file, else a declared service whose id is slug(info.title), else the package or service that owns the description's directory, else the system. It is removed when nothing is left in it.
- Inside an external part, endpoints nothing requests are dropped.
- Viewer: a glyph for kind api; in the details "Described in openapi.yaml:12 · createOrder · CreateOrder → Order".

title: A call counts as resolved by a code index when the index has a call of that name on its line
description: docair-4wk.37: with a SCIP index, a call the index cannot resolve now gets could lines from the syntax. The adapter tells them apart by (line, name): a syntax call whose name matches a call the index lists on the same line is the index's; the rest are read by the syntax (could lines only, never a certain line, since the index's answer stands). On docair it added 31 lines. TypeScript drew could lines already with or without its index, so it needed no change. Alternative: compare by column, which SCIP has and the syntax reading would need too.

title: A call over [code] max_candidates is an error, E007
description: docair-4wk.34/4wk.36: 'if the limit does not hold, it is a rendering error'. Decided: a diagnostic of severity error (E007, so docair check fails), at the call's file and line, naming the call, the method name, how many functions fit and the limit, with what to do (raise it, 0 for all, -1 for none). On docair itself none at the default 5. Alternative: a warning, so a project with many shared names still checks clean.

title: A flow renamed is matched only when the match is clear
description: docair-zrr.32: a flow only A has and one only B has are one renamed flow when they are of the same kind, each is the other's only candidate, and they share at least half of each one's parts (by B's ids). Two candidates, or less in common, stay one gone and one new. Alternative: match the best one among several.

title: The review's pieces keep their stretches; only the page's flow walk goes part by part
description: docair-zrr.35 asked for one step per part in a changed flow's walk. change_steps::steps also makes the review's pieces (review::pieces), so changing it would cut every review into one piece per part. Decided: a new change_steps::part_steps does the walk, one step per new, gone or code-changed part, plus a step for a new or gone line between two unchanged parts (else it would not show); the review keeps steps' stretches and forks. Alternative: pieces by part too, which gives the AI many more, smaller pieces.

title: A changed Helm value is tested as a manifest's Service selecting another Deployment
description: docair-zrr.34 asked the two-commit test to cover a changed Helm value (another Service selected). The infra adapter resolves .Values only in names, images and ingress classes, not in a Service's selector, so a Helm value there would show no change at all. Decided: the test changes a manifest instead (an Ingress routed to a new Service that selects another Deployment), which is what such a value does. To follow up: resolve .Values in selectors and backends, then test the Helm form.

title: A commit's graph is built once per process, never read from disk
description: docair-zrr.30: comparisons take no graph from a cache, since a kept one may no longer be right. But docair serve --changes writes its page again on every file change, and building commit A in a worktree each time would cost a full scan. Decided: a graph built in this process is kept in memory (commits::BUILT, by commit, docair's version, the commit's docair.toml and leniency) and used again; a commit's files and the running docair cannot change, so it is never stale. The graphs are written to .docair/changes/graphs/<commit>.graph.json for a reader, never read back. The code index (SCIP) stays kept by its sources' content, which is always right. Alternative: build every time, also in one process.

title: docair serve notices reviews only in the default store inside its own folder
description: docair-8l6.74: serve ignores its output folder when it watches files; reviews now go to .docair/changes by default. Decided: a JSON file directly in <root>/.docair/changes counts (watched, files_seen), what lies below it does not (the commit graphs of docair-zrr.30 go there). A store configured elsewhere in the project is watched as any project file; one configured elsewhere inside .docair is not noticed until the next rewrite.

title: A change's picture brings at most 12 parts one line away from each of its parts
description: docair-8l6.77 adds one step around a change's picture, faded. A part used widely (a central type, a hub function) has dozens of neighbours and would flood the picture. Decided: at most review::AROUND = 12 neighbours a part, in the graph's edge order, no test's covers line; the picture's own focus for big pictures (zrr.28) still applies. Alternative: all neighbours, or rank them (calls before reads).

title: Built tasks are committed locally group by group, not pushed
description: The user asked to build all 26 tasks of the decision review without stopping and to commit what was uncommitted. Decided: each group of tasks is committed locally once its gates and e2e pass, so the other session can take its files back; nothing is pushed until the user asks.

title: docair's own reviews already in docs/changes stay; new ones go to .docair/changes
description: docair-8l6.74 moves the default store to .docair/changes. docair's repository has six reviews committed in docs/changes (the AI's reviews of its own work). Decided: they stay as they are, as a record, and docair's docair.toml does not set store, so new reviews go to .docair/changes and are not committed. Alternative: set store = docs/changes for docair itself and keep committing them.

title: The last request still places a left piece named by a part it holds
description: docair-8l6.81 made the review's how strict: only a piece's own id binds, the rest goes back to the model once. The last request's place (docair-8l6.56) still finds a left piece by a part it holds or a part in its box (resolve_left), without a repair request: what it misses becomes a change in docair's words anyway. To follow up: make it strict too, with or without a repair.

title: A part's code link opens the repository host at a commit, the editor for the working tree
description: docair-8l6.82 left open what a link to a part's file opens. Decided (commits::code_links): a commit opens on its repository host at that commit's sha, from the origin remote, GitHub (https://github.com/o/r/blob/<sha>/<path>#L<line>) and GitLab (/-/blob/); ssh and https remotes both, a token in one never kept. The working tree opens in VS Code (vscode://file/<root>/<path>:<line>), since its uncommitted text is on no host. Another host, or no remote: the file and line show alone. Alternatives: a setting choosing host, editor or none; other hosts (Bitbucket, Gitea) by pattern.

title: While the review's one request runs, the page shows a moving bar, not answered requests
description: With one request (docair-8l6.79) there are no parts to count. The job's html shows an indeterminate progress bar while it runs, the words 'The AI reviews n pieces · k changes so far · time', and each change as it is made; done, a full bar.

title: Walkthroughs keep 'written by hand'; only the review's hand corrections went
description: docair-8l6.75 drops hand corrections from the review (recorded.by human on a stored change). The task also named page_walks' 'written by hand': that labels walkthroughs a person wrote (docs/walkthroughs/*.json with recorded.by human), a separate feature the decision was not about. Decided: keep it.

title: Generated files stay out of what the AI gets: lock files, the beads export, review stores, binaries
description: docair-8l6.79 sends everything that changed, nothing cut, and left open whether generated files go too. Decided: they stay out as before (commits::not_for_the_ai): they are not the change's code, a lock file alone can be larger than the whole review, and the review store would review itself. Alternative: send them too, at the cost of the size limit.

title: A stored review that covers every piece is kept as stored, whoever edited the file
description: With hand corrections gone (docair-8l6.75), docair no longer looks at recorded.by: a stored review is kept as it is while its changes and other cover exactly today's pieces, and asked again whole when they do not. A person can still edit the file, and the edit lasts until the pieces change. Alternative: ask again on every run; costs a request each time nothing changed.

title: [explain] max_requests is still read, and ignored
description: docair-8l6.79 makes a review one request, so max_requests has no meaning. The settings reject unknown keys (deny_unknown_fields), so removing it would make a docair.toml that sets it fail to load. Decided: keep it as an accepted key that does nothing, documented as no longer used. Alternative: remove it and let such files fail with an error naming it.

title: The review's one request is streamed, so each change still shows as soon as it is whole
description: docair-8l6.79 makes a review one request; docair-8l6.65 wanted each change shown as soon as it is complete. Decided: the request asks the endpoint to stream (stream: true, server-sent events, client::chat_streamed), and explain::complete_changes takes each change object once its closing brace has arrived; it is bound and goes out with the progress, and the whole answer is bound as before at the end. An endpoint that rejects stream, or answers without it, is read whole. Timeouts: 15 minutes to the first byte (a long input is read first), 60 minutes in all. Alternative: no streaming, the changes all at once at the end.

title: Changes: a changed flow's walk has one step per new, gone or changed part
description: Decision docair-zrr.25, reviewed and changed: a changed flow is still walked with the page's walk player (docair-zrr.24, kept), but each step is now one part: every new, gone or code-changed part is its own step, in the flow's order, with its lines, at a size to read. Stretches, forks as one step and the 8-part split by box go. Long walks for big changes are accepted.

title: Changes: the two-commit tests cover a rerouted request, a Helm value, removals and several additions

title: Changes: a changed docair.toml is shown first, as what it changed
description: Decision docair-zrr.10, reviewed and changed: each commit is still read with its own docair.toml; when the two differ, the changes show that first and plainly: the docair.toml lines that changed (sources, hide rules, adapter settings) and that some differences may come from them. Graphs are never taken from a cache (docair-zrr.30), so a different docair version can no longer be the reason.
close_reason: GraphDiff.toml: docair.toml's changed lines, first in the changes and the summary; tests a_changed_docair_toml_is_its_lines, a_changed_docair_toml_comes_first; e2e 71/71, docair check 0/0

title: Changes: a comparison builds both commits fresh, and writes their graphs to .docair/changes
description: Decisions docair-zrr.11 and zrr.10, reviewed: a comparison never takes a graph from a cache; both commits are built fresh each time, since a kept graph may no longer be right. The graphs a comparison builds are written to the project's .docair/changes, beside the reviews (docair-8l6.74), where a reader can find them (e.g. .docair/changes/graphs/<commit>.graph.json), but never read back to save a build. The user's cache folder (graphs/<key>.json) goes. To settle when building: the exact layout, that docair serve's watcher ignores it, and whether the code index (SCIP, kept by its sources' content) counts as such a cache too.

title: Code: could lines also for the calls a code index cannot resolve
description: Decision docair-4wk.33, reviewed and changed: with a SCIP index for a file, a call the index resolves keeps the index's answer, and a call it cannot resolve now gets could lines from the syntax reading (the candidates by name, at most [code] max_candidates), as files without an index do. Measure on docair: how many could lines that adds.

title: Code: [code] max_candidates sets how many could lines a call may draw, default 5
description: Decisions docair-4wk.32 and 4wk.34, reviewed and changed: the Rust adapter's MAX_CANDIDATES = 5 becomes [code] max_candidates in docair.toml, default 5, read by the Rust and TypeScript adapters. -1 turns guesses off: no could lines at all. 0 shows every candidate, however many. N > 0 draws could lines to at most N candidates; a call with more than N is not left silently undrawn: it is reported as a rendering error (a diagnostic docair check and the page's problems show, naming the call, its method name and how many candidates it has). Docs: ADAPTERS 5.5, SPEC's docair.toml reference and diagnostics.

title: Pictures: a line's words show whole, with room made for them
description: Decision docair-702.34, reviewed and changed: a picture no longer cuts a line's words to two lines with '…'; they show whole, wrapped at 28 columns, and the layout makes room for them (rows sized for their tallest words, as layered.rs sizes each gap). Crowded words still show on zoom (docair-702.35). Pictures grow: measure on docair's page (picture area, words covering parts) before and after. Every kept layout runs again once, and the golden SVGs move.

title: Build: layout.wasm is built in CI, not committed
description: Decision docair-702.26, reviewed and changed: crates/docair-layout-wasm/layout.wasm leaves the repository. CI builds it (wasm32 target) and the release, the Docker build and the e2e use that build; a devcontainer gets the wasm32 target to build it locally. The test that compares the committed file with the router's version goes, or checks the built file instead.

title: Layout: a box shrinks to fit when a moved part leaves it
description: Decision docair-702.25, reviewed and changed: move_part grows a box to hold a moved part and now also shrinks a box a part left to fit what stays in it, with the default room. A box edge that would then cut through a line routed before: route that line again (as move_part does for the moved part's lines), so no box crosses a line.

title: Layout: a moved part's lines keep off the lines that stayed
description: Decision docair-702.24, reviewed and changed: docair-layout's move_part routes the lines touching a moved part around every part and now also around the lines that stay: they occupy their tracks in the router before the moved lines are routed, so a moved line no longer runs along a staying one and their words do not meet. Lines the reader did not touch still do not move.

title: CLI: only docair build; the scan alias goes
description: Decision docair-702.23, reviewed and changed: one name for the command that writes the page and the graph. Every mention of docair scan becomes docair build (CLAUDE.md's build section, the README, CI, e2e, docs, the CLI's help and tests), and the scan alias is dropped from the CLI.

title: Review: how much the model reasons first is [explain] reasoning, default low
description: Decision docair-8l6.36, reviewed: reasoning_effort for the review becomes a setting, [explain] reasoning = low | medium | high, default low (GLM-5.3-Flash on Together reasons until max_tokens runs out without it). An endpoint that rejects reasoning_effort still gets the request without it.

title: An earlier question's refs are told to the model in today's words
description: docair-rgz keeps a question's refs in the history; ask::messages turns them into words again for each later question (ask_context::about on the current graph), not the words the model got then. The review of 99b30eb flagged it as a risk: after a rescan the history describes parts with today's facts. Decided: keep it. The model answers about the graph as it is now, the words stay short (refs, not text), and a ref that names nothing now is simply left out. Alternative: store the words as sent with each turn; more to keep in the page's session, and stale after a rescan.

title: A found off stored before the kinds is a contradiction when it says what was said, else a risk
description: Reviews stored before docair-8l6.62 have offs without a kind: source commit/doc/comment with what was said, or source none (or a bare sentence), which the old prompt asked for as 'what the code does and why that is a problem' and the page showed as 'Nothing: no commit, doc or comment mentions it'. Decided: on reading, one that says what was said is a contradiction; the rest is a risk (FoundOff::kind, page_changes::off_item), so old none-items now show under 'Looks wrong or risky', not 'Done, but said nowhere'. Why: the old none mixed both, and the items stored were risks (docair's own c1364fd..work review: all three); 'said nowhere' would bring back the mislabel 8l6.62 fixed. Commit 906ed6f's message says 'Stores without kinds read as before', which overstates this: they read, but their none-items change heading. Alternative: map them to unsaid, exactly as they were labelled; rejected for the mislabel.
close_reason: Reviewed: decided by the user; kept as built

title: An inserted doc block goes between a struct's attributes and the struct
description: With the real model, 'Document docair-cli.cli.' gave an insert edit whose block lands below #[derive(...)] and #[command(...)] and right above 'struct Cli {' (edit::resolve uses the node's code line). It compiles and docair binds it, but doc comments belong above an item's attributes. Fix: an insert above a Rust item goes above the attribute lines that lead into it (as review::leads_into finds a part's leading lines).
notes: Built: edit::insert_block walks above an attribute or decorator that spans lines (#[command( … )], @Component({ … })), finding the line it opens on with its brackets balanced, at most 40 lines up; a line that only ends in a bracket with no attribute above it keeps the block where it was. Test: edit::tests::a_block_goes_above_an_attribute_that_spans_lines.

title: A review asked in parts tells each request the others' pieces, and leaves to them what it names of them
description: docair-8l6.60: asked in parts, the model reads the commit messages and docs every request gets and names pieces of other requests, so most problems were that, and a change holding only such pieces was lost. Decided: each request's input ends with the ids of the pieces the other requests hold, to leave out of 'how'; before binding, a 'how' entry that names one of those (or a part only they hold) is dropped, and a change left with nothing goes; each request says this once as a problem ('request 3: 5 of its pieces were another request's, left to it'). A split review reserves room for the list in each request (the pieces' ids, at most half of MAX_CHARS). Alternative kept open: keep such a change for the last request to merge into the one that holds its pieces, so its why and found off are not lost; follow up if real runs lose changes this way.

title: A sent question takes its Ask-about chips along; the selection's chip stays
description: docair-rgz left open whether the chips above the question clear once it is sent. Decided: the chips put in with ✦ Ask about this go with the question, into its bubble, and leave the box above the question, so each question says what it was about and the next starts empty. The chip of the selected part stays while the part is selected, as before: it follows the selection, not a question. title: Found off: a piece id in the code sentence reads as 'path:orders.audit'
description: With the real model on the shop, an off's code sentence names the piece (path:orders.audit) where the part (orders.audit) belongs: 'path:orders.audit is an empty function body'. Piece ids are known ids, so bind keeps them, and the card and comment show the piece id. title: Decision: a commit is read from a git worktree; B may be the working tree
description: docair diff <A> [<B>] adds a detached git worktree per commit in a scratch folder and removes it afterwards; without B the working tree is B. CHANGES.md §7 rows 1 and 2.
close_reason: Reviewed: kept as built

title: Decision: Follow is made readable by laying slices out without shrinking, and opening at the first step
description: docair-tqy listed three options to discuss. Decided (the user asked for decisions to be taken and recorded): (a) a slice is laid out without top-down shrinking (Options budget infinite, floor 1), so nested boxes no longer multiply 0.7 and every word keeps its size; the picture grows and the reader pans; (b) Follow opens at the walk's first step with the step camera (0.8 to 1.3 screen px per unit) instead of the whole picture fitted. Not chosen: folding a datum's slice to the lines that carry it (it would hide the way the datum takes, which is what Follow is for). To revisit: whether layers and sections should also stop shrinking.
close_reason: Reviewed: kept as built

title: Decision: a call with too many candidates lists nothing yet
description: ADAPTERS §5.5 says a call with more candidates than the limit draws no lines and its details list them. Rust and TypeScript draw nothing and list nothing: the graph has no place for a call that names no line, and a list of 6 to 50 methods by name is noise more often than help. To revisit: an inferred note on the caller (calls m: 12 methods of that name) shown in its details.
close_reason: Reviewed: changed, folded into docair-4wk.36 (-1 off, 0 all, past the limit an error)

title: Decision: could lines: the candidate limit is a constant 5, not yet a [code] setting
description: ADAPTERS §5.5 names [code] max_candidates (default 5). The Rust adapter uses MAX_CANDIDATES = 5 and has no setting yet: no project asked for another number. To revisit: add max_candidates to [code] when one does.
close_reason: Reviewed: changed, becomes a setting (docair-4wk.36)

title: Decision: could lines only without a code index
description: With a SCIP index for the file, the index's answer stands and calls it cannot resolve get no could line; could lines come only from the syntax path (uploads, projects without rust-analyzer). To revisit: add could lines for the index's unresolved method calls too.
close_reason: Reviewed: changed, could lines for unresolved calls too (docair-4wk.37)

title: Could lines in TypeScript, and the candidates of a call with too many in its details
description: Left from docair-4wk.13: the Rust adapter draws could lines for x.m(…) of unknown type; the TypeScript adapter does not yet (plain JavaScript, any, obj[name]()), and a call with more than the limit of candidates draws nothing and lists nothing (ADAPTERS §5.5 says the details list them). Design: docs/ADAPTERS.md §5.5.
notes: Built (TypeScript): crates/docair-lang-ts/src/lib.rs Reader::calls records x.m(…) on anything but this (FileRead.could); link() gives one Reach::Could line to each class method of that name in the project (never the caller itself), 1 to MAX_CANDIDATES (5), unless the platform's objects have the name (JS_STD_METHODS: map, then, emit, subscribe, querySelector, …). Test a_method_of_unknown_type_could_be_each_of_that_name (two save methods: two could lines; map: none). On docair: no could line (its TypeScript calls go through this.field or platform names). Goldens unchanged; docair check 0/0. Not done: listing the candidates of a call with too many (decision issue).
close_reason: TypeScript could lines are in; the list of too many candidates is a decision to go over.

title: Decision: a page opened from disk offers the tidy command, not the patch
description: The viewer does not read the project's files, so a page opened as a file cannot make the diff: it shows the repeated tags and the command docair tidy --apply; the patch comes from GET /api/tidy when docair serve or a kept upload answers. To revisit: let docair build write docair.patch beside the page and link it.

title: Decision: in and out tags from or to a part count as repeated when the code says the same
description: @in x: T from p and @out x: T to p are hand-written data lines; when the code infers the same line with the same words before from/to, tidy removes them (two on docair: discover and extract). A @in or @out without from/to is a signature and never touched. To revisit: keep data lines the author wrote even when the code says them, as documentation of the datum's name.
close_reason: Reviewed: kept as built

title: Decision: repeated tags are worked out on demand, not stored in the graph
description: ADAPTERS §6.1 said every scan puts the repeated tags into the graph as proposed edits. docair_core::tidy::repeated works them out from the graph when asked (docair tidy, the hint, the page, /api/tidy), so the graph's schema and the golden graphs stay as they are. To revisit: store them if a consumer of docair.graph.json needs them.
