title: Decision: the page's WASM module is kept built in the repository
description: crates/docair-layout-wasm/layout.wasm is committed with the code version it was built from; a cargo test fails when docair-layout changed and the script was not run. The Docker build, CI and every devcontainer then need no wasm32 target. To revisit: build it in CI, or in a build.rs, once a wasm32 target is there anyway.
close_reason: Reviewed: changed, built in CI (docair-702.42)

title: Decision: a moved part's lines avoid every part, not the lines that stayed
description: docair-layout's move_part routes only the lines touching the moved part, around every part; the lines that stay are not obstacles, so a moved line may run along one of them, and the words of moved lines may meet the words of others. Routing all lines again would move lines the reader did not touch. To revisit: make the lines that stay obstacles in the router (occupy their tracks) before routing the moved ones.
close_reason: Reviewed: changed, staying lines become obstacles (docair-702.40)

title: Decision: a box only grows when a part inside it is moved
description: move_part grows each box around a moved part to hold it again with the default room (Options::default().padding, scaled by the box), and never shrinks a box a part left. To revisit: shrink to fit, which can make the box cut through lines routed before.
close_reason: Reviewed: changed, shrink to fit (docair-702.41)

title: Decision: docair scan stays as another name of docair build
description: docair build is the command (the user's word for the on-demand path); scan stays a visible alias, because CLAUDE.md, the README, CI, e2e and the docs use it. To revisit: rename every mention and drop the alias, or keep both.
close_reason: Reviewed: changed, only build (docair-702.39)

title: docair ask and docair chat make the question too: @creates data.question
description: On docair's own graph, data.question's slice has 6 stretches of their own. Several of them start in docair-cli: docair ask takes the question from its argument and docair chat from each line typed, but only the web chat panel says @creates data.question. Add @creates to cmd_ask and cmd_chat in crates/docair-cli/src/ask.rs, so the slice reaches those lines from where the question is made.

The line main → cmd_ask is still a stretch of its own: main hands the argument on.

title: Viewer: the code as a dependency matrix, a view beside the Code picture (prototype for review)
description:
A prototype was built for review outside the repository, generated from docair's own graph (1302 parts, 2071 lines). It is not in the viewer yet. Rows and columns are the code tree (libraries and programs, crates, modules, functions), opened level by level. A cell counts how often its row uses its column: calls, reads and writes, tests. Each box's parts are ordered so that what is used comes first (Tarjan's strongly connected parts, the used ones first). A mark above the diagonal therefore runs against the order: a cycle or a step back up.

Numbers: it works out any level in under 1 ms and draws in 2-8 ms, where the Code picture takes 12 s. At 1 level in: 125 parts, 685 lines, 85 lines against the order, 3 cycles.

What it shows on docair today:
- viewer.js sits in two places (74 lines). The TypeScript adapter files 227 functions under the docair-viewer crate (docair-viewer.assets.viewer), and the 31 documented ones sit under docair-viewer.page. Calls between them cross the two, and form a cycle.
- docair-core.adapter.collect calls every language adapter through the Adapter trait, while the adapters use core: a cycle of 6 crates.
- The web app's App and ResultView call each other.

Choices made in the prototype: data lines are off by default, because they follow the data (f's result handed to g) and answers would read as cycles. Read lines are turned around, so the reader is the row. Lines between two parts outside the code are left out. Outside the code is split into who uses the code and what it uses.

To decide: whether the viewer gets the matrix as a view (a switch at Code, or a layer of its own); its design doc in docs/; whether walks and the search work on it; whether 'against the order' and the cycles become diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria: A decision after review. If yes: a design doc in docs/, then the matrix in the viewer with an e2e test, drawn in under 100 ms on docair's page.
notes: CLI side (this session): crates/docair-core/src/matrix.rs matrix(graph, opened) -> Matrix { rows (id, name, depth, holds, side used/code/uses), cells (row, col, count), against, cycles }: each level (the system, each opened box) ordered by Tarjan, what is used first, what the code uses before it and who uses it after; reads turned, data lines and lines between two outside parts left out. docair matrix [--open id] prints it. Test what_is_used_comes_first_and_a_cycle_runs_against_the_order. On docair: 6 rows, 344 lines, 69 against, 1 cycle (browser, docair-lib, workstation); docair-lib and docair-apps opened: 18 rows, 527 lines, 79 against, 2 cycles. SLICES §7a, SPEC CLI table. Left: the view in the page (the other session), decided below.
close_reason: Dropped: the user decided the matrix is not needed (2026-11-19). The CLI side built earlier (docair_core::matrix, docair matrix, SLICES §7a, SPEC row, meanings entry) was removed again before it was committed.

title: Infra: from a Service to the program its pods run (image, Dockerfile, crate or app)
description: Left from docair-4wk.21: k8s.svc.docair-server -> docair-server.router, k8s.svc.docair-web -> nginx, nginx -> docair-web.main are hand-written only. The code says it in steps: the Service selects the Deployment (inferred); the Deployment's image is {{ .Values.server.image.repository }}:{{ tag }} (values.yaml, now read: docair-server:dev); Terraform builds that tag from docker/server.Dockerfile; the Dockerfile builds the crate (cargo build -p docair-server) or copies the app (web dist into nginx's root); the crate's main binds the port the Service targets and serves the router. Read Dockerfiles (FROM, COPY, RUN cargo build -p, EXPOSE) and the image tags Terraform builds, then link Service -> the entry that serves (the router, nginx).
acceptance_criteria: On docair, Service docair-server -> docair-server.router and Service docair-web -> nginx come from code; --coverage counts them.
notes: Built: crates/docair-lang-infra/src/lib.rs: K8sObject.images (container image:, filled from the chart values by fill_values); Index.dockerfiles (docker_build: RUN cargo build -p crate, COPY of project files, not --from), Index.builds (docker_builds in Terraform resource lines: docker build -f … -t …, locals expanded, by image repository), Index.mains (Cargo.toml [package] name with a src/main.rs gives crate.main); in a Service selection, program_of(image) gives a certain call to the crate main, else to the part a copied file documents. On docair: k8s.svc.docair-server -> docair-server.main and k8s.svc.docair-web -> nginx come from code (the authored router line is behind main calling router; the nginx line is confirmed). Test a_service_reaches_the_program_its_pods_run (fixtures.rs). ADAPTERS §5.7 and §7. Goldens unchanged; docair check 0/0.
close_reason: A Service reaches the program its pods run, from the image, the Dockerfile and the crate or copied config.

title: Stores that say where they are: certain file lines from paths the code writes out
description: Option (b) of docair-4wk.18: today a file read or write (file:) only confirms the store a block names (§5.7). A store block that says where it is (new tag, e.g. '@path docs/walkthroughs/*.json' or '@path .env') lets code that writes the path out (literal, const, config default) get a certain @reads/@writes without a block on the function. Needs a SPEC tag, resolve matching file:<path> against the stores' globs, and the adapters keeping literal paths (they do: file:.env).
acceptance_criteria: A store with @path and a function reading that literal path give a certain line with no @reads on the function; SPEC documents @path; a fixture.
notes: Built: @path <glob> (known tag, check.rs; SPEC tag table): crates/docair-core/src/resolve.rs bind_open_refs binds an inferred file:<path> to the stores whose @path fits (path_stores, path_fits: * within a segment, ** any segments, ./ and trailing / ignored, the glob's folder fits) before asking the blocks; certain for one store, one-of for several. Tests: paths_fit_store_globs, a_file_the_code_names_binds_to_the_store_that_says_its_path (resolve), a_store_with_a_path_is_read_by_the_code_that_names_it (fixtures.rs, through the Rust adapter: fs::read_to_string("data/shop.json") reads the store @path data/*.json with no block on the function). docair's stores got their @path (walkthroughs, glossaries, meanings, test reports, .env); its code builds those paths at run time, so no new line. ADAPTERS §5.7. docair check 0/0.
close_reason: Stores say where they are with @path; code naming a fitting path gets a certain line.

title: Layout worker: check Firefox and Safari, and test stopping a layout on a large picture in e2e
description:
The layout worker (docair-c5a, @id docair-viewer.layout-worker) has only been checked in Chromium: from file://, over HTTP, and in the web app's sandboxed srcdoc frame. Firefox and Safari are not installed in the devcontainer. Things to check there: a Blob worker made by an opaque-origin document (the web app's frame), and OffscreenCanvas text measurement that matches the page's (otherwise the picture differs). Where the worker does not start, the viewer lays out on the page as before (workerFailed), so nothing breaks, but the page freezes again on large pictures.

The e2e fixtures are too small to test the two things that matter on large pictures: that a click on another layer stops a running layout, and that no frame waits longer than 100 ms. They were measured by script on docair's own page (frame gaps of 20 ms during a 23 s Code layout, Apps drawn 0.78 s after the click).
acceptance_criteria: The page lays out in the worker in Firefox and Safari, from file:// and in the web app, with the same picture as on the page. An e2e fixture, or a generated large graph, lets a test stop a running layout with a layer click and check the frame gaps.
close_reason: Obsolete since docair-702.5: the page has no layout worker; it lays out nothing.

title: Infra: the network entry from code (host port, kind node, ingress controller)
description: 15 hand-written lines describe how a request gets in: browser -> host port -> kind node -> Traefik -> Ingress, plus ConfigMaps and the AI endpoint. The infra adapter reads Ingress -> Service -> Deployment but not the entry: kind_cluster's extra_port_mappings (host_port -> container_port) in Terraform, the ingress controller's Service (NodePort) in its Helm values, and which controller takes the Ingress (ingressClassName is read).
acceptance_criteria: On docair, host port -> kind node -> Traefik -> Ingress comes from Terraform and the chart values; the open scenario's network steps keep their paths.
notes:
From the coverage analysis: also Service -> the program behind it (k8s.svc.docair-server -> docair-server.router; k8s.svc.docair-web -> nginx -> docair-web.main): a Service's targetPort meets the port the program listens on (axum bind, nginx listen) and the files nginx serves.
Built 2026-11-18 (crates/docair-lang-infra): tf_subs() reads blocks inside resources (node, extra_port_mappings, values = [yamlencode(...)]) with attributes and parents; flat_values()/from_values() read a chart's values.yaml and resolve {{ .Values.x }} (Ingress class); ids_at maps documented code lines to their block @id. sub_relations(): mapping -> its node (TCP host -> :container), node -> the release values whose nodePort it publishes, controller values (ingressClass/isDefaultClass) -> Ingresses of its class. Ingress paths with port: name: keep their Service (bug: only number: closed a path, so /api -> docair-server was lost). Tests: the_way_into_the_cluster, ingress_paths_with_named_ports. ADAPTERS §7.1, SPEC §6. docair: 185 of 218 (84%); calls missing 16 -> 12 (host-port -> kind-node -> k8s.traefik -> k8s.ingress.docair now from code; ingress -> svc.docair-server too). Left: Service -> program (docair-4wk.26).
e2e 2026-11-18 (npm test, whole tree): 59 passed, 0 failed. Workspace tests, clippy, fmt clean; docair check . 0/0.
close_reason: Host port -> kind node -> ingress controller -> Ingress from Terraform and chart values; Ingress paths with named ports; Service -> program left as docair-4wk.26

title: Rust adapter: more than one item on a line
description: items_by_row keeps only the outermost item per line, so in 'impl Adapter for A { fn file(&self) {} }' or 'mod config { pub fn load() {} }' on one line the inner fn has no symbol: no node, no calls to or from it, and an index definition on that line maps to the impl. Found while writing step 7's tests; real code rarely does it, rustfmt never.
acceptance_criteria: Items that share a line each get a symbol and their calls; attaching blocks still goes to the item the block's code line starts.
notes: Built: crates/docair-lang-rust/src/lib.rs items_within_rows: items that start on the line of an item around them (fn file in impl A { fn file() {} }, fn load in mod config { … }) are read too, after the outer one; the first item on a line keeps the key rust:<file>:<line>, the ones inside get :<column>; FileRead::at(Within) takes the innermost of items on the same lines, so a call starts at the function; the index's definitions (functions only) map to the inner function because it is listed last. Test items_on_one_line_are_parts_of_their_own. Goldens unchanged; docair check 0/0. Also fixed two resolve unit tests the W122 change broke (their databases are stores now).
close_reason: Several items on one line each get a part, and calls start at the innermost.

title: Walks use request lines
description: request::link (step 6) adds the lines of requests after resolve, but resolve already computed the scenario paths (flow_paths), so a @flow scenario cannot step along a request line made from code. On docair itself nothing changes, because its scenarios walk the network path. With the hand-written @calls host-port removed, the upload scenario breaks (W104 at step 3 -> 4).
acceptance_criteria: A scenario whose steps are linked only by a request line from code has a path (no W104); docair's own scenarios unchanged; goldens unchanged.
notes: Built: crates/docair-core/src/lib.rs scan computes resolve::flow_paths after request::link (resolve returns nodes and edges only; link only appends lines and word_and_prune changes no line's index, so the paths stay valid). Test a_walk_steps_along_a_request: a @requests POST /api/orders and its handler, two @flow steps, no W104, step 2 goes along the request line. Goldens unchanged; docair check 0/0.
close_reason: Scenarios step along request lines made from code.

title: Apps layer: nginx is drawn as one of docair's programs
description:
On docair's own page, the Apps layer draws nginx as a program, next to docair-cli, docair-server, docair-web and the viewer page. But nginx is off-the-shelf software. In docair it only serves docair-web's built files, inside the docair-web container (docker/web.Dockerfile, docker/nginx.conf). The repository holds its config, not its code.

Why: the doc block in docker/nginx.conf declares `@id nginx`, `@kind service`, `@part-of container.docair-web`. SPEC §3.4 says a program is a `service` or `job` that is not inside another program and not declared in Terraform. The viewer follows that rule (crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js: classify marks every such node `program`; appPart puts every program on Apps). So by the current rule, nginx is a program.

Compare Traefik, also off-the-shelf: it is declared as a `gateway` (k8s.traefik, infra/terraform/ingress.tf), and the Apps layer leaves gateways out.

Two walks pass nginx: `open` (step 7) and `provision` (step 11). Whatever changes, they must still show it.
design:
Options:

| Option | What changes | Effect |
|--------|--------------|--------|
| Declare nginx as a `gateway`, or another kind that Apps leaves out | the doc block in docker/nginx.conf | nginx shows on Network; Apps shows docair's own programs |
| A program needs its code in the repository (a manifest such as Cargo.toml or package.json); a service declared only by a server's config file is not one | SPEC §3.4, classify in viewer.js | every project with an nginx, Redis or Traefik config gets the same |
| Keep it as it is; SPEC says why a server like nginx is a program | SPEC §3.4 | none on the page |
acceptance_criteria: The choice is made and written down (in SPEC §3.4, or in the doc block). docair's own Apps layer shows what it says. The walks open and provision still show nginx at their steps. docair check . stays at 0 errors and 0 warnings.
notes:
Built 2026-11-18, option 1:
- docker/nginx.conf: @kind gateway (was service). The block now says why: nginx is off-the-shelf, like Traefik.
- docs/SPEC.md, kinds table: `gateway` also covers software the project only configures, such as a web server (nginx).

On docair's own page:
| Layer | nginx |
|---|---|
| Apps | left out; the programs are docair-cli, docair-server, docair-viewer.page, terraform, docair-web |
| Network | drawn as itself (before: its Deployment stood for it) |
| Kubernetes | drawn as itself, as before |
| Infrastructure | inside the namespace box, as before |
| Code | left out |

- Apps loses the lines browser → nginx (GET /) and nginx → docair-web (the bundle). The request still bridges to docair-web, but docair-web sits inside the browser box, so no line is drawn. The way in still shows at Network and in the open walk.
- Walks: open plays at Network, and step 7 shows nginx itself (before: its Deployment box). provision plays at Infrastructure; its step 11 sits in step 8 "Inside namespace docair", with nginx in the namespace box, as before.
- The line nginx → docair-web.main carries data.page, and Code now leaves nginx out. The viewer session (data walks) knows.

Validation: docair check . has 0 errors and 0 warnings; e2e 53/53 passed.
close_reason: nginx is now a gateway (docker/nginx.conf), as Traefik is, so the Apps layer shows only docair's own programs. It is drawn as itself on Network and Kubernetes, the walks open and provision still show it, the SPEC kinds table says why, and docair check . is at 0 errors and 0 warnings.

title: Meanings: a @defines tag, and words that name no part
description: docs/MEANINGS.md §10, left out of epic docair-xkj: (1) a tag such as '@defines facts' lets an author settle a word in the code instead of docs/meanings.toml; (2) words that name no part (NodePort, CIDR) are found only by the model, not by docair check; (3) an entry the reviewer drops comes back on the next explain run. Design first, as an addition to MEANINGS.md.
notes: Built (design in MEANINGS.md §10): (1) @defines word, word (known tag; SPEC tag table): meanings::settle takes it as a decision from = that part, the decisions file wins. (2) meanings.unnamed: words written like names (CamelCase, 3 to 6 capitals, _ kept inside variables, HTTP methods left out) used in 2 or more texts outside code spans, with no part (CamelCase compared by its words), entry or decision; at most 20; the explain run asks for entries of those a reader needs. On docair: SPEC, JSON, HTML, TypeScript, ConfigMap, YAML, … (17). No warning. (3) Decision.proposed: every entry the model writes is marked; a marked word without an entry is not proposed again (docair-ai glossary). Tests: a_defines_tag_settles_a_word_in_the_code, words_that_name_no_part_are_found. shop.graph.json blessed: meanings.unnamed ["API"]. docair check 0/0.
close_reason: @defines, words that name no part, and dropped entries remembered.

title: Rust adapter: //! docs of a module file are the module's docs
description: docs/MEANINGS.md §10: the Rust adapter reads /// docs of an item, not the inner //! docs of a module file. crates/docair-core/src/facts.rs says '//! Facts: what adapters learn from the code', which would define *facts* by itself (MEANINGS.md §2) without a decision. When a mod item has no block and no /// docs, take the module file's //! docs as its summary and description.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture module with only //! docs gets them as its summary; a word it defines ('X: …') settles without a decision; goldens that move say why.
notes: Built: crates/docair-lang-rust/src/lib.rs inner_docs(text): a module file's first //! lines or /*! */ comment (attributes and blank lines skipped, stops at the first item); a mod x; item without /// docs takes them as its docs (the module file found by module_file, read from the project root). A docair block above the mod still wins. Test a_module_files_inner_docs_are_read. On docair: docair-layout.draw, .text and .hand_move now carry their //! summaries; no golden moved; docair check 0/0. MEANINGS §10 updated.
close_reason: A module file's //! docs are the mod item's docs when it has none of its own.

title: Following data: say what the walk covers, keep its lines lit, mark data in step titles
description:
When a data walk is short or shows only some of the lines that carry the datum, nothing says so: the card says 'Step 1 of 1', Play and Next do nothing, and it looks as if nothing happened. The lines that carry the datum are not lit while the walk plays (SPEC §3.6 says they stay lit). Step titles name the maker and the datum the same way ('ask.digest makes digest'), which reads like a typo when they share a name.
How to tackle: in the walk's card, say how many lines carry the datum and how many the walk shows, and list the others (for example 'carried by 16 lines; 4 are in this walk, 12 more below'); keep the carrying lines lit during the walk; mark the datum with ◇ in step titles ('ask.digest makes ◇ digest'). Smaller once the reply fix (docair-nkm) lands, since walks then reach more lines.
acceptance_criteria: A data walk that cannot show every carrying line says so in its card and lists the rest; the carrying lines drawn on the layer stay lit while the walk plays; step titles mark data with ◇.
notes: Built (viewer, crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js + viewer.css): (1) The walk card's first step says what the walk covers. carriedLines (@id docair-viewer.data-cover) writes 'Carried by N lines, all in this walk; K of them start stretches of their own, not reached from where it is made.'; it lists lines not in the walk, if any, and the lines this layer does not draw (at most 8, then '… N more'; ends named with nameOf). (2) Lit lines: the carrying lines stay teal (--data, 3.5 px, opacity 1) while the walk plays. applyFollow no longer fades the walk's own parts and lines: the maker, and the lines it travels inside, used to get carry-dim (opacity 0.18). Selected parts are never carry-dimmed (.carry-dim:unselected). (3) The walk's words mark the datum with ◇: 'ask.digest makes ◇ digest', 'brings ◇ reply back', 'Not reached from where ◇ X is made'. Data chips no longer match the end of a dotted part name ('ask.digest'). On docair's page: digest 'Carried by 1 line, in this walk.'; reply 'Carried by 23 lines, all in this walk; 4 of them start stretches of their own…'; at Apps reply lists 17 lines not drawn. Tests: e2e/tests/data.spec.ts checks the card line, ◇ titles, lit lines and no carry-dim on the walk's parts (shop and answer fixtures). e2e 53/53; docair check 0 errors, 0 warnings. SPEC §3.6.
close_reason: Data walk cards say what the walk covers and list what the layer does not draw; carrying lines stay lit and the walk's parts never fade; the walk's words mark data with ◇.

title: Viewer: the data kind has no colours (console warnings, empty legend swatch)
description: The viewer's style gives every entry of KINDS a fill and an outline from viewer.css (crates/docair-viewer/assets/viewer.js, makeStyle: --k-<kind>-bg and --k-<kind>-line), but viewer.css has no --k-data-bg or --k-data-line. So every page logs two Cytoscape warnings when it loads ('The style property `background-color: ` is invalid', and the same for border-color), and the legend's '◇ data' entry shows an empty swatch (transparent fill). Data parts are never drawn on the canvas (they have their own list, SPEC §3.6), so nothing else shows it. Seen on docair's own page and on the e2e fixture pages. Fix: define the two colours for data in viewer.css (light and dark), or leave data out of the canvas style and colour its legend swatch directly.
acceptance_criteria: A page loads with no console warnings; the legend's data entry shows a coloured swatch in light and dark mode.
notes: docair-702.4: the SVG pictures give data the data colours (pictures.css: .k-data uses --data-soft and --data). The viewer.js page keeps its two Cytoscape warnings until docair-702.5 replaces it; close then.
close_reason: Superseded by docair-702.5: viewer.js and its Cytoscape style are gone; the pictures and the legend give data the data colours.

title: axum nest("/prefix", router): prefix the routes of a nested router
description: Step 4 reads .route(...) and method chains, but not nest(). No code in docair or the fixtures uses nest, so it was left out instead of guessed. Needs a Rust-side rule (escape hatch, ADAPTERS.md §5.2): follow the nested router from a variable or a function that returns it, and prefix its routes (core route::join from docair-4wk.6.1).
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with Router::new().nest("/api", api()) where api() has .route("/scan", post(h)) gives serves http POST /api/scan by fn h.
notes: Built: crates/docair-lang-rust/src/lib.rs nests_of (tree-sitter: .nest("/p", f()) names the function building the router; .nest("/p", x) the let x = … before it in the same function), route_prefixes (each nested function's prefix, nests in nests joined with docair_core::route::join; a let's lines), and in link_with the serves facts and the router's call payloads on those lines or in those functions get the prefix. Test nested_routers_put_their_prefix_in_front (GET /api/orders, /api/v1/items/{id}, /admin/users, /healthz unprefixed; payloads too). ADAPTERS §5.2. Goldens unchanged; docair check 0/0.
close_reason: axum nest prefixes are composed: by function, by variable, nests in nests.
